Deterministic spec assembly, validation legibility, and the advisory grouper

trouble run r20260828-220035 · git range a2098a08..93dadc02 · pull request

Ship waves 1a–1c of the grouper-speccer-flow requirements so that after this run the grouper is the well-working core of the planning→run flow: - **Wave 1a** (R1, R2, R4, R21, R22, R23 + superseded R3): `group` produces a launchable `groups.json` with **zero LLM calls** — specs assembled deterministically from the plan's own unit sections — and worker context is layered (shared digest + per-group full sections) instead of every worker carrying the full plan. The grouping-time speccer is **deleted** (ADR 0006), not made opt-in: R3 is superseded by the grill decision of 2026-08-28. - **Wave 1b** (R5–R11): the six measured validation-legibility failures (C1–C6 in `docs/todos/grouping_improvements.md`) are fixed so a written plan never again costs 15 `group` invocations to validate. - **Wave 1c** (R12–R15): `group --advise` — multi-granularity comparison and plan-cohesion diagnostics off one built graph, zero LLM — plus the merge-key fill penalty, and `/orchestrator-plan` consulting the advisory before asking the user about splits. Waves 2–3 (mechanical split R16, deepen R17–R19, eval harness R20) are out of scope. A **post-eval-harness backlog** section at the end records what waits.

Summary

Deterministic spec assembly, validation legibility, and the advisory grouper — r20260828-220035

TL;DR

This is the re-run of the plan and partition that run r20260828-212053 abandoned when its first group failed terminally. Two fixes in the launch commit gave a clean 1410-outcome baseline, and the same eleven groups then ran unattended for about 2h45m.

  • All 11 groups completed and merged on generation 1; base a2098a08 to tip 93dadc02, PR opened (g1)
  • Zero-LLM-call spec assembly and the advisory grouper both landed as specced, closing R1 (R1)
  • Legibility work (validation errors, contract labels) shipped across the run's later groups (g6)

Problems found

Five findings, none of them blocking: two are design deviations the coders documented in their own reports, two are gaps a group worked around, and one is a merge-gate hole the run exposed rather than caused.

  • g4's plan-cap bucketing read as a mathematically redundant no-op; implemented as a distance-from-target-fill term instead, see groups/g4/report-g1-r1.json (g4) The coder argued the case in its report rather than silently diverging, which is the behaviour the ground rules ask for.
  • g6's upstream/downstream contract labels missed pure implements/consumes pairs with no direct dependency edge; added a separate tag-matching pass, see groups/g6/report-g1-r1.json (g6)
  • g7 did not find ADR 0006, referenced by its spec as required reading, and proceeded from the plan's Decisions section instead, see groups/g7/report-g1-r1.json (g7)
  • g7 found speccer.py's write_specs()/GroupSpec still live for the rewrite speccer and relocated rather than deleted them, see groups/g7/report-g1-r1.json (g7)
  • The merge gate runs pytest only: g7's TypeScript changes merged with zero UI verification because the check command never reaches package.json when uv markers exist (ui/src/routes/Launch.tsx) The launch-commit baseline is pytest-only for the same reason, so a UI regression is invisible on both sides of the comparison.

Run notes

No escalations, no respawns, no usage-limit pauses: the driver's work was the launch, the watch, and an independent verification of the integration branch that the gate's pytest-only check never performed for the UI.

  • This is the re-run of the same plan and partition after run r20260828-212053 died at g1; the two fixes in the launch commit gave a clean 1410-outcome baseline and g1 merged first try (a2098a08)
  • No escalations, no respawns, no usage-limit pauses: every group merged on its first coder generation, about 2h45m wall clock (g1/coder/gen1)
  • Checked g7's UI changes by hand against the integration branch since the gate never ran them: 199/199 vitest and a clean tsc (ui/src/types.ts)
  • Verified the integration branch independently: 1482 pytest passed against 1410 on main, ADR 0006's speccer deletion confirmed, --price and --advise exercised live (93dadc02)
  • The four over-budget groups (g3, g7, g10, g11) all landed on generation 1 without tripping the 250k breaker, so the estimator's over-budget flag is conservative rather than predictive (g7)

Next steps

Ordered by the damage each does if left: the gate hole first, since it makes every UI change in every future run unverified, then the two plan-prose corrections that stop the next plan from repeating the same misreadings.

  • Make the merge gate run the UI suite alongside pytest: today a TypeScript regression is invisible on both sides of the baseline comparison; done means a compound check command, the baseline captured by that same command, and a UI-only red merge refused (ui/src/routes/Launch.tsx)
    • how: make [preflight] check_command a list or a compound command in config.toml and reuse it for baseline capture, so the two sides stay comparable
  • Correct the boolean-bucket framing in the plan prose before U12 is revisited: the redundant no-op reading is what the g4 coder had to argue past; done means the plan states the distance-from-target-fill term the code implements, before the eval harness tunes it (g4)
  • Verify no other unit assumed speccer.py's removal was a pure deletion: write_specs()/GroupSpec are still live for the rewrite speccer; done means every consumer of the relocated symbols is checked and ADR 0006's wording matches what actually remains (g7)

base-context.md (898 lines)

Base context

Worker ground rules

These rules apply to every coder and reviewer session forked from this base context, for the spec you will be given below and the plan document that follows it.

For coders

  • Work only inside your worktree (your current working directory); never touch paths outside it.
  • Your worktree owns its own environment: dependency changes require uv sync run inside the worktree, and any verification item that imports a new dependency must pass there, in that worktree — never against the parent checkout's environment.
  • Implement the spec you are given fully — code and tests — following the conventions established above.
  • Commit early and often: after each self-contained step that leaves the worktree in a consistent state (a finished file, a passing unit of work), make a git commit with a clear conventional message. Do not accumulate large uncommitted work — if your session is interrupted, only committed work survives; anything uncommitted is lost when the group restarts. The commit subject must start with the first character of the type, not whitespace — if you're using a heredoc to pass the message, check the exact bytes, since a leading newline or space before the subject line is a common heredoc mistake.
  • If a command is denied for permissions, retry the identical command up to three times total, then stop and report status permission_denied with the denied command verbatim in denied_command. Re-sending the identical command is not a workaround; alternate quoting, alternate spellings, shelling through another interpreter, and subprocess.run substitution for the same command are all banned — they route around the sandbox instead of reporting the block.
  • Verify your work against the verification items you will be given before reporting.

For reviewers

  • Compute the diff yourself from git rather than trusting the coder's report: verify claims against the actual code and run the tests the spec calls for.
  • If you need scratch space, use only the directory the round names for it, and do not leave scratch files anywhere else in the worktree — the merge gate requires a clean tree.

Report block rules (both roles)

Every final message ends with EXACTLY ONE <run-report> block, whose body is valid JSON with no trailing commas and no comments, and nothing after the closing tag.

  • A coder's status attribute is one of completed | blocked | failed | needs_input | permission_denied and must match the JSON body's "status" field.
    • Use needs_input only when a decision only a human can make blocks you (an ambiguous requirement, a product trade-off, missing access). Put the single specific question in a top-level "question" field; the run pauses and resumes you with the operator's answer. Do not use it for anything you can resolve yourself.
    • Use permission_denied only after retrying the identical denied command up to three times total. Put the exact command in a top-level "denied_command" field, verbatim, with no paraphrasing or quoting changes. Do not use it for a blocked report — that status is unrelated to permission denials.
    • With permission_denied, also set two top-level fields that say how it was denied, because three unrelated causes look identical from where you stand and each needs a different fix from the operator:
      • "denial_error": the error text you actually saw, verbatim — do not summarize or rephrase it. If nothing came back at all, write exactly no error text was returned; a stated absence is usable, a blank field is not.
      • "denial_source": "tool_refused" if the tool call was refused and the command never ran, or "command_error" if the command ran and failed. You know which one happened and the orchestrator cannot work it out afterwards, so this is the single most useful thing you can report here.
    • Every verification item you were given must appear in "verification_results" with status pass | fail | skipped.
  • A reviewer's status attribute is one of approved | changes_required | too_hard | structural and must match the JSON body's "status" field.
    • approved: the work satisfies the spec and its verification items.
    • changes_required: fixable within this group — list concrete, actionable items in "required_changes".
    • too_hard: the spec cannot be satisfied by iterating here; escalate for a spec rewrite.
    • structural: the group boundaries themselves are wrong (work belongs to or conflicts with another group).
  • Either role may record a surprise: a finding that likely invalidates another group's assignment — an interface mismatch, a missing dependency, work that belongs elsewhere. Record it instead of fixing it yourself: {"kind": "interface_mismatch" | "missing_dependency" | "merge_conflict" | "other", "description": "...", "affected_groups": ["g2"]}

Repo conventions (CLAUDE.md)

smart-mcps

A Claude Code plugin that installs skills and session hooks for codegraph, NotebookLM, and Perplexity.

Plugin structure

This is a Claude Code plugin repository. Hooks and skills are distributed to plugin consumers via auto-discovered files:

Path Purpose
hooks/hooks.json Plugin-level hook registrations (uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT})
hooks/scripts/ Hook implementation scripts (.py and .sh)
skills/ Skill definitions
agents/ Subagent definitions (auto-discovered; .claude/agents symlinks here for local dev)
codegraph_mcp/ FastMCP proxy exposing 6 trimmed codegraph tools (smart-mcps-codegraph)
.mcp.json MCP server registration — serves plugin consumers and local dev (see below)
.claude-plugin/plugin.json Plugin identity (name, version)
.claude/settings.json Project-level hooks for local development (uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)

Adding hooks — always register in both places

Every hook script must be wired up in two files:

  1. hooks/hooks.json — so plugin consumers receive it. Uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.
  2. .claude/settings.json — so it runs locally during development. Uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

Matchers are case-sensitive and PascalCase in both files (e.g. "Edit|Write|MultiEdit", "Bash") — a lowercase matcher silently matches nothing. This applies to every event, including SessionStart (codegraph reindex, formatter bootstrap), not just PostToolUse.

Registering in only one place means either plugin consumers or local dev is broken. Always do both.

MCP servers — one file, not two

The dual-registration rule above does not apply to MCP servers: .claude/settings.json has no mcpServers key (it only approves servers via enabledMcpjsonServers). A single .mcp.json at the repo root covers both audiences, because Claude Code reads it twice:

  • Plugin consumers — auto-discovered as the plugin's ./.mcp.json; tools resolve as mcp__plugin_smart-mcps_codegraph__<tool>.
  • Local dev — read as the project-scoped .mcp.json; tools resolve as mcp__codegraph__<tool>.

Hence "--project", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}". ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is set only for consumers; locally it falls back to . (the server's cwd is the project root). Two constraints worth knowing before editing that line:

  • ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is not available in .mcp.json — only in hooks. Using it yields a "Missing environment variables" warning.
  • Defaults don't nest. ${VAR:-default} works, but ${A:-${B}} does not expand B — it silently passes a literal, which uv may accept when the console script is already on PATH, hiding the bug locally while breaking for consumers.

Never keep working notes in the /tmp scratchpad

The session scratchpad under /tmp is wiped when the Claude Code process restarts — not just at the end of a session. Anything written there is gone without warning.

This has already cost real work: on 2026-07-29 a restart destroyed the accumulated findings and deferred-fix list for two sessions of orchestrator debugging, plus a patch backup of a group's stranded work.

Use /tmp only for genuinely throwaway intermediates. Anything another session would want — findings, deferred-fix lists, handoff notes, backups of uncommitted work — goes somewhere durable:

what where
Run findings, deferred fixes, backups .orchestrator/ — gitignored, survives restarts, never collides with a group merge
Facts worth recalling across sessions the auto-memory dir (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/)
Anything the repo should carry docs/ — committed

Write it durably as you go, not at the end. A restart gives no notice.

title: Deterministic spec assembly, validation legibility, and the advisory grouper type: feat date: 2026-08-28 origin: docs/brainstorms/2026-08-28-grouper-speccer-flow-requirements.md

Deterministic spec assembly, validation legibility, and the advisory grouper

Objective

Ship waves 1a–1c of the grouper-speccer-flow requirements so that after this run the grouper is the well-working core of the planning→run flow:

  • Wave 1a (R1, R2, R4, R21, R22, R23 + superseded R3): group produces a launchable groups.json with zero LLM calls — specs assembled deterministically from the plan's own unit sections — and worker context is layered (shared digest + per-group full sections) instead of every worker carrying the full plan. The grouping-time speccer is deleted (ADR 0006), not made opt-in: R3 is superseded by the grill decision of 2026-08-28.
  • Wave 1b (R5–R11): the six measured validation-legibility failures (C1–C6 in docs/todos/grouping_improvements.md) are fixed so a written plan never again costs 15 group invocations to validate.
  • Wave 1c (R12–R15): group --advise — multi-granularity comparison and plan-cohesion diagnostics off one built graph, zero LLM — plus the merge-key fill penalty, and /orchestrator-plan consulting the advisory before asking the user about splits.

Waves 2–3 (mechanical split R16, deepen R17–R19, eval harness R20) are out of scope. A post-eval-harness backlog section at the end records what waits.

What we already know (resolved context)

Ground truth verified 2026-08-28 against the working tree (commit d141d6e):

  • The speccer call being deleted is write_specs (orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py:62), invoked once by run_grouping (orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py:673) with per-group skeletons {tasks, descriptions, files} and the stripped plan text. Its output type GroupSpec carries group_id, name, summary (≤120 chars, SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS in orchestrator/model.py), spec, verification: list[VerificationItem]. VerificationItem is {id, description, required} (orchestrator/model.py:32). The prompt template is orchestrator/prompts/speccer.md.
  • Two speccers exist: the grouping-time one above (deleted) and the mid-run rewrite speccer (orchestrator/cli.py:1919 _rewrite_provider area, orchestrator/execution/review.py escalation path, run-form knob model_speccer in ui/src/components/launch/ExecutionOptions.tsx:261). The rewrite speccer, the run-form knob, and the Observatory LLM-call viewer (SpeccerCalls in ui/src/components/grouping/GroupingTab.tsx) all stay. The grouping-form knob (GroupingOptions.model_speccer, orchestrator/observatory/launch.py:121/147, ui/src/routes/Launch.tsx:193, grouping-form parts of ui/src/types.ts:532) goes.
  • compute_partition (pipeline.py:436) is the deterministic sub-second prefix: parse map → quiescence → graph → partition → group DAG; it returns PartitionOutcome with graph, partition, dag, node_work, budget_cap, hub_roles, slice_atoms, flags, base_context, base_tokens. run_grouping adds estimator + speccer and builds Group objects. serialize_grouping is the canonical groups.json writer.
  • Base context today embeds the full plan: compile_base_context (orchestrator/grouping/base_context.py:19) = ground rules + CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md + codegraph summary + strip_task_map(plan). It is byte-stable by contract, feeds start_base (orchestrator/execution/sessions.py:400), which loads it into the run's base session that all workers fork from — so "shared block first in every worker prompt" (R23) is already the architecture; only the content changes.
  • Budget arithmetic: node_work (orchestrator/grouping/estimator.py:51) = source_bytes/bytes_per_token(4.0) × slack_multiplier(1.3) + file allowances (per_file_tool_allowance, 2000; size_hints 500/2000/5000); partition_budget_cap (estimator.py:79) = token_budget(200,000) − head, head = (base_tokens + spec_tokens_allowance) × slack × coder_slack_multiplier(2.5). The trace records this as BudgetArithmetic (pipeline.py:526).
  • C1 confirmed live: _check_slice_overflow (pipeline.py:214) raises on the first over-cap slice inside its loop; plan_reader.py has ~20 raise TaskMapError sites and no accumulator.
  • Merge key confirmed (orchestrator/grouping/partition.py:974): (-source_wave, candidate_makespan, -removed_affinity, -edge_weight, merged_work, source, target) — merged_work is a 5th-place tiebreaker with no fill/balance term, matching the R19b greedy-fragmentation finding.
  • Advisory building blocks exist: _simulate_makespan (partition.py:783), _compute_waves (partition.py:998), compute_scorecard + _modularity (orchestrator/grouping/scorecard.py), Granularity/GRANULARITY_LEVELS (partition.py:40), the preview/ quarantine for --no-spec/--dry-run (cli.py:665–742), EdgeProvenanceRecorder/edge_provenance_document (pipeline.py:306), _drop_inferred_cycles (graphing.py:626 — task-graph level only; the group-DAG repair repair_cycles in partition.py merges SCCs and re-splits by wave, never withdraws inferred edges).
  • Plan-unit conventions: unit headings are ### U<N>. <name>; task ids are u<N>-<slug>. strip_task_map (plan_reader.py:133) removes the fenced map block and its ## Task Map heading from embedded copies only.
  • Symbols stay empty in this plan's own map (R9/C4 lesson): on this dense codebase populating symbols added 103 inferred precedence edges and degenerated the partition; declared depends_on and shared-file affinity carry the structure instead.
  • config.session.speccer_model powers the mapper LLM (foreign plans) and the rewrite speccer as well as the grouping speccer — the field and --model-speccer survive the deletion; only their grouping-time consumer goes, and help text is reworded.

Decisions

  • Delete the grouping-time speccer; keep the rewrite speccer and the Observatory LLM-call viewer. (→ ADR 0006) The planner session is the speccer; the paraphrase added cost and drift surface, not information. Deletion is one standalone commit, recorded in docs/orchestrator-grouping.md for cherry-pick recovery. Rejected: opt-in overlay (its enrichment dies on re-group; deepen in wave 2 is the durable path), deleting the rewrite path (it consumes genuinely new failure history — out of wave-1 scope).
  • Dry deterministic prose is acceptable (brainstorm decision, unchanged): names/summaries derived from unit titles, relational header from graph facts only (R2) — no polish pass.
  • Verification items come only from the plan. Assembled verbatim from unit Verification bullets with stable ids <group_id>-<n>, required=true. LLM-added verification happens in deepen (wave 2), written into the plan.
  • Layered context is the default, not a flag. Shared digest = plan preamble (everything before ## Units, task map stripped) + one tagged Summary: line per unit + implements/consumes registry. Group spec = member units' full sections verbatim + relational header + contracts-only lines for cross-group neighbors. No worker receives the full plan. Rejected: keeping the full plan in base context behind a flag (defeats R22's token economy).
  • R11 is edge withdrawal only. repair_cycles withdraws inferred precedence edges (never declared ones) on the group DAG before merging. The hyperedge/hub-routing re-modeling of symbol edges is parked to the post-eval-harness backlog (user decision 2026-08-28).
  • The fill-penalty experiment lands in wave 1c (user decision 2026-08-28): a fill/balance term promoted in the merge key so one group stops absorbing merges until it hits the cap; --advise's granularity comparison is the immediate before/after readout.
  • Verification-coverage lint in wave 1a (user decision 2026-08-28): after assembly, every unit Verification bullet must appear as a VerificationItem in exactly one group; a miss is a hard GrouperError naming the unit.
  • No cross-invocation graph cache for --advise in v1 (user decision 2026-08-28): the three granularity partitions reuse one built graph within a single invocation; re-run latency is measured first, cached later only if needed.
  • --price compiles its cap estimate without codegraph and labels it approximate: base context is compiled with an empty codegraph summary, so the printed cap is within a few thousand tokens of the real one, sub-second, with the delta stated in the output.
  • Advisory thresholds are named constants, tuned during implementation on the existing runs/traces in this repo (brainstorm open question resolved as "tune in 1c"): near-disconnected WCC edge-weight threshold, seriality depth/width ratio, cut-sweep valley detection, and the low-modularity / high-conductance "structurally monolithic" report.

U1. plan-sections — deterministic plan parsing: unit sections, summaries, digest

  • Goal: A parser that splits a plan document into (a) the preamble (everything before the ## Units heading, task map stripped), (b) unit sections keyed by unit id — heading ### U<N>. ↔ task ids matching u<N>-… — each with its verbatim body, its tagged Summary: line, and its parsed Verification bullets, and (c) a digest builder producing the shared block: preamble + per-unit tagged summary lines + implements/consumes registry. Parse errors accumulate per phase and report together (same discipline as R5). A unit with no Summary: line falls back to its heading title with an info flag (older plans keep working); a task id with no matching unit section is a hard error.

Thresholds are named module constants. --advise follows preview semantics: never touches a persisted groups.json.

Post-eval-harness backlog (do not implement now)

Recorded per the 2026-08-28 grill so nothing is lost when the R20 eval harness lands (post-Infinity-Skills):

  • Hyperedge / hub-routing re-modeling of symbol-derived edges (R19b): model dense shared symbols as affinity hyperedges or route them through the hub machinery at graphing time instead of pairwise precedence — one of the first experiments to run against the eval harness. Until then U10's withdrawal is the mitigation.
  • dagP-style acyclicity-safe refinement pass (moving nodes back out of oversized groups) — the pipeline currently has no refinement stage; U12's fill penalty is the cheap precursor whose effect the harness should measure.
  • Cross-group read-overlap-aware merging (brainstorm non-goal): pricing shared read context across candidate merges.
  • Fill-penalty calibration: target_fill_ratio's default is a judgment call in U12; the harness's estimator-calibration metric should tune it.
  • --advise cross-invocation graph cache keyed by (plan sha, index fingerprint) — only if measured re-run latency violates R14 in practice.

g1: deterministic-spec-assembly

u1: plan-sections — deterministic plan parsing: unit sections, summaries, digest

Plan section U1

U1. plan-sections — deterministic plan parsing: unit sections, summaries, digest

  • Goal: A parser that splits a plan document into (a) the preamble (everything before the ## Units heading, task map stripped), (b) unit sections keyed by unit id — heading ### U<N>. ↔ task ids matching u<N>-… — each with its verbatim body, its tagged Summary: line, and its parsed Verification bullets, and (c) a digest builder producing the shared block: preamble + per-unit tagged summary lines + implements/consumes registry. Parse errors accumulate per phase and report together (same discipline as R5). A unit with no Summary: line falls back to its heading title with an info flag (older plans keep working); a task id with no matching unit section is a hard error.
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/plan_sections.py (new, large), tests/test_plan_sections.py (new, medium)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: —
  • Slice: assembly
  • Implements / Consumes: implements plan-sections
  • Verification:
    • Parsing this plan document itself yields one section per task-map entry, each section's text found verbatim in the source, and a digest that contains every unit's Summary: line and none of the unit bodies.
    • A plan whose unit U3 heading is missing while the map declares u3-layered-context raises one error naming u3-layered-context, and a plan with two missing sections reports both in the same error.
    • The digest and section split are byte-stable: parsing the same text twice yields identical bytes.
    • The task-map YAML block appears in neither the digest nor any section.

u2: spec-assembly — assemble group specs deterministically, replacing write_specs

Plan section U2

U2. spec-assembly — assemble group specs deterministically, replacing write_specs

  • Goal: run_grouping builds every group's name, summary (within the 120-char cap), spec, and verification with zero LLM calls: name/summary derived from member unit titles; spec = a generated relational header (member list with descriptions, intra-group depends_on in topological order, upstream/downstream groups with the contract tags exchanged, slice membership — graph/DAG facts only, per R2) followed by the member units' plan sections verbatim; verification = the units' Verification bullets with ids <group_id>-<n>, required=true. The verification-coverage lint runs after assembly: every unit bullet lands in exactly one group or GrouperError names the unit. groups.json gains the flag specs: assembled from plan — speccer LLM skipped. The stage progress line becomes stage: assemble (no per-spec LLM progress).
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/assembler.py (new, large), orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py, tests/test_assembler.py (new, medium), tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: u1-plan-sections
  • Slice: assembly
  • Implements / Consumes: consumes plan-sections; implements assembled-specs
  • Verification:
    • group on a task-mapped plan completes with an LLM runner stub that raises on any call (_llm_must_not_be_called-style), and the produced groups.json validates against GroupingResult with non-empty name/summary/spec/verification for every group.
    • Each group's spec contains its member unit sections verbatim, and its relational header names exactly the upstream/downstream group ids that build_group_dag produced — regenerating after a changed partition changes the header accordingly (R2).
    • Every Verification bullet of every unit appears as exactly one VerificationItem across all groups, ids matching ^g\d+-\d+$; removing one unit's Verification section makes grouping fail naming that unit.
    • groups.json output is byte-deterministic across two runs on an unchanged repo.
Spec given to this group

Implement U1 (u1-plan-sections) and U2 (u2-spec-assembly) from the plan — the foundation of wave 1a. Read those two unit sections in the plan document for the authoritative goals; this spec covers how they fit together and what constrains you.

U1 first, U2 on top of it. U1 is a new module orchestrator/grouping/plan_sections.py: a pure parser over a plan document producing (a) the preamble — everything before the ## Units heading with the task map stripped (reuse strip_task_map in orchestrator/grouping/plan_reader.py:133), (b) unit sections keyed by unit id, matching heading ### U<N>. to task ids u<N>-…, each carrying verbatim body, the tagged Summary: line, and parsed Verification bullets, and (c) a digest builder emitting preamble + one tagged summary line per unit + the implements/consumes registry. A unit with no Summary: line falls back to its heading title and raises an info flag — older plans must keep working. A task id with no matching unit section is a hard error. Parse errors accumulate per phase and report together (the same discipline U6 applies elsewhere; U6 is a sibling group, so implement accumulation locally here rather than waiting on shared helpers).

U2 is a new orchestrator/grouping/assembler.py plus the run_grouping wiring in orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py:673, which today calls write_specs. Replace that call with deterministic assembly: name and summary derived from member unit titles (summary within SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS, orchestrator/model.py); spec = a generated relational header followed by the member units' plan sections verbatim; verification = the units' Verification bullets as VerificationItems with ids <group_id>-<n> and required=true. Per the plan's R2 decision the relational header uses graph/DAG facts only — member list with descriptions, intra-group depends_on in topological order, upstream/downstream group ids with the contract tags exchanged, slice membership — no interpretive prose. Dry deterministic prose is explicitly acceptable; do not add a polish pass and do not call an LLM anywhere in this path.

After assembly run the verification-coverage lint: every unit Verification bullet must land in exactly one group's VerificationItems, otherwise raise GrouperError naming the unit. Add the flag specs: assembled from plan — speccer LLM skipped to groups.json and change the stage progress line to stage: assemble with no per-spec LLM progress.

Constraints. Do not delete orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py or orchestrator/prompts/speccer.md — a separate group (U4) owns the removal commit; just stop calling write_specs from the assembled path. GroupSpec/VerificationItem shapes stay as they are. serialize_grouping remains the canonical writer; groups.json must be byte-deterministic. compute_partition's deterministic prefix is unchanged.

Done means group on a task-mapped plan produces a launchable groups.json with a runner stub that raises on any LLM call, the coverage lint is live, and tests/test_plan_sections.py, tests/test_assembler.py, and the updated tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py are green alongside the existing suite.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

1"""Deterministic spec assembly (plan U2): replaces the grouping-time speccer.
2
3The planner session already wrote the prose that matters — a paraphrase pass
4over it added cost and drift surface, not information (ADR 0006). Every
5group's name, summary, spec, and verification are built here from graph/DAG
6facts and the plan's own unit sections, with zero LLM calls.
7"""

28def _truncate_summary(text: str) -> str:
29 text = " ".join(text.split())
30 if len(text) <= SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS:
31 return text
32 return text[: SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS - 1].rstrip() + "…"

35def _topo_order(members: list[str], graph: TaskGraph) -> list[str]:
36 """Member tasks in dependency order (Kahn's algorithm over the intra-group
37 subset of ``graph.dependencies``); ties broken lexicographically for
38 determinism."""
39 member_set = set(members)
40 indegree = {m: 0 for m in members}
41 downstream: dict[str, list[str]] = {m: [] for m in members}
42 for up, down in sorted(graph.dependencies):
43 if up in member_set and down in member_set:
44 indegree[down] += 1
45 downstream[up].append(down)
46 ready = sorted(m for m in members if indegree[m] == 0)
47 ordered: list[str] = []
48 while ready:
49 node = ready.pop(0)
50 ordered.append(node)
51 for down in sorted(downstream[node]):
52 indegree[down] -= 1
53 if indegree[down] == 0:
54 ready.append(down)
55 ready.sort()
56 # A cycle inside one group is unreachable (build_group_dag already asserts
57 # acyclicity at the group level, and intra-group cycles can't exist without
58 # one) — but never silently drop a node if it somehow happened.
59 ordered.extend(m for m in members if m not in ordered)
60 return ordered
61

63def _member_label(task_id: str, unit: UnitSection | None, description: str) -> str:
64 if unit is not None:
65 return unit.title
66 return description or task_id

69def _group_name(ordered_members: list[str], units: Mapping[str, UnitSection | None]) -> str:
70 labels = [
71 _member_label(task_id, units.get(task_id), "") or task_id for task_id in ordered_members
72 ]
73 return " + ".join(labels) if labels else "empty group"

76def _group_summary(ordered_members: list[str], units: Mapping[str, UnitSection | None]) -> str:
77 if len(ordered_members) == 1:
78 task_id = ordered_members[0]
79 unit = units.get(task_id)
80 text = unit.summary if unit is not None else task_id
81 return _truncate_summary(text)
82 labels = [
83 _member_label(task_id, units.get(task_id), "") or task_id for task_id in ordered_members
84 ]
85 return _truncate_summary(f"{len(ordered_members)} units: " + ", ".join(labels))

88def _relational_header(
89 gid_str: str,
90 name: str,
91 ordered_members: list[str],
92 graph: TaskGraph,
93 units: Mapping[str, UnitSection | None],
94 descriptions: Mapping[str, str],
95 upstream_labels: list[str],
96 downstream_labels: list[str],
97 slice_label: str | None,
98) -> str:
99 lines = [f"# Group {gid_str}: {name}", ""]
100 lines.append("Members:")
101 for task_id in ordered_members:
102 unit = units.get(task_id)
103 label = unit.title if unit is not None else descriptions.get(task_id, task_id)
104 lines.append(f"- {task_id}: {label}")
105 lines.append("")
106
107 intra_edges = sorted(
108 (up, down)
109 for (up, down) in graph.dependencies
110 if up in ordered_members and down in ordered_members
111 )
112 lines.append("Intra-group order (depends_on):")
113 if intra_edges:
114 for up, down in intra_edges:
115 lines.append(f"- {up} before {down}")
116 else:
117 lines.append("- (no intra-group dependencies)")
118 lines.append("")
119
120 lines.append("Upstream groups:")
121 if upstream_labels:
122 lines.extend(f"- {label}" for label in upstream_labels)
123 else:
124 lines.append("- (none)")
125 lines.append("")
126
127 lines.append("Downstream groups:")
128 if downstream_labels:
129 lines.extend(f"- {label}" for label in downstream_labels)
130 else:
131 lines.append("- (none)")
132 lines.append("")
133
134 lines.append(f"Slice: {slice_label or '(none)'}")
135 lines.append("")
136 return "\n".join(lines)

147class AssemblyInputs:

157def assemble_group_specs(inputs: AssemblyInputs) -> dict[str, GroupSpec]:
158 """Build every group's ``GroupSpec`` with zero LLM calls (plan U2).
159
160 Raises ``AssemblyError`` if a unit that maps to a task actually present in
161 this partition has no Verification bullets — a hard signal the plan lost
162 its verification section, not something assembly can paper over.
163 """
164 units = inputs.plan_sections.units
165 unit_by_task: dict[str, UnitSection | None] = {
166 task_id: section_for_task(units, task_id)
167 for members in inputs.members_by_gid.values()
168 for task_id in members
169 }
170
171 upstream_of: dict[int, list[int]] = {gid: [] for gid in inputs.members_by_gid}
172 for up_gid, downs in inputs.dag.items():
173 for down_gid in downs:
174 upstream_of[down_gid].append(up_gid)
175
176 specs: dict[str, GroupSpec] = {}
177 covered_unit_ids: set[str] = set()
178
179 for gid, members in sorted(inputs.members_by_gid.items()):
180 gid_str = inputs.group_label(gid)
181 ordered_members = _topo_order(sorted(members), inputs.graph)
182 name = _group_name(ordered_members, unit_by_task)
183 summary = _group_summary(ordered_members, unit_by_task)
184
185 member_set = set(members)
186 upstream_labels: list[str] = []
187 for up_gid in sorted(upstream_of[gid]):
188 up_gid_str = inputs.group_label(up_gid)
189 for task_id in sorted(inputs.members_by_gid[up_gid]):
190 for up, down in sorted(inputs.graph.dependencies):
191 if up == task_id and down in member_set:
192 unit = unit_by_task.get(task_id)
193 implements = unit.implements if unit is not None else ()
194 tag = implements[0] if implements else task_id
195 upstream_labels.append(
196 _contract_label(up_gid_str, task_id, unit, tag, "provides")
197 )
198 downstream_labels: list[str] = []
199 for down_gid in sorted(inputs.dag.get(gid, ())):
200 down_gid_str = inputs.group_label(down_gid)
201 for task_id in sorted(inputs.members_by_gid[down_gid]):
202 for up, down in sorted(inputs.graph.dependencies):
203 if down == task_id and up in member_set:
204 unit = unit_by_task.get(task_id)
205 consumes = unit.consumes if unit is not None else ()
206 tag = consumes[0] if consumes else task_id
207 downstream_labels.append(
208 _contract_label(down_gid_str, task_id, unit, tag, "consumes")
209 )
210
211 slice_labels = sorted(
212 {str(inputs.graph.metadata.get(task_id, {}).get("slice") or "") for task_id in members}
213 - {""}
214 )
215 slice_label = ", ".join(slice_labels) if slice_labels else None
216
217 header = _relational_header(
218 gid_str=gid_str,
219 name=name,
220 ordered_members=ordered_members,
221 graph=inputs.graph,
222 units=unit_by_task,
223 descriptions=inputs.descriptions,
224 upstream_labels=sorted(set(upstream_labels)),
225 downstream_labels=sorted(set(downstream_labels)),
226 slice_label=slice_label,
227 )
228
229 body_parts = [header]
230 verification: list[VerificationItem] = []
231 counter = 0
232 for task_id in ordered_members:
233 unit = unit_by_task.get(task_id)
234 if unit is not None:
235 body_parts.append(unit.text)
236 covered_unit_ids.add(unit.unit_id)
237 for description in unit.verification:
238 counter += 1
239 verification.append(
240 VerificationItem(
241 id=f"{gid_str}-{counter}",
242 description=description,
243 required=True,
244 )
245 )
246 else:
247 body_parts.append(f"### {task_id}\n\n{inputs.descriptions.get(task_id, '')}\n")
248
249 specs[gid_str] = GroupSpec(
250 group_id=gid_str,
251 name=name,
252 summary=summary,
253 spec="\n\n".join(body_parts),
254 verification=verification,
255 )
256
257 _lint_verification_coverage(units, unit_by_task, covered_unit_ids)
258 return specs

261def _lint_verification_coverage(
262 units: Mapping[str, UnitSection],
263 unit_by_task: Mapping[str, UnitSection | None],
264 covered_unit_ids: set[str],
265) -> None:
266 """Every unit that maps to a task actually present in this grouping must
267 have contributed at least one Verification item to some group."""
268 present_unit_ids = {unit.unit_id for unit in unit_by_task.values() if unit is not None}
269 for unit_id in sorted(present_unit_ids):
270 unit = units[unit_id]
271 if not unit.verification:
272 raise AssemblyError(
273 f"unit {unit_id} ({unit.title!r}) has no Verification bullets — "
274 "every grouped unit must contribute at least one verification item"
275 )
276 if unit_id not in covered_unit_ids:
277 raise AssemblyError(
278 f"unit {unit_id} ({unit.title!r}) contributed no VerificationItem "
279 "to any group — this is an assembler bug"
280 )

orchestrator/grouping/plan_sections.py
@@ -0,0 +1,230 @@
1"""Deterministic plan-document parser: preamble, per-unit sections, and the
2shared digest that replaces embedding the full plan in worker context (R1, R21,
3R22, R23).
4
5A plan written for ``orchestrator-plan`` has a ``## Units`` section whose
6sub-headings are ``### U<N>. <name> — <goal>``. Task ids of the form
7``u<N>-<slug>`` are this convention's task-map counterpart to heading ``U<N>``.
8Older or foreign plans (no ``## Units`` heading, or task ids that don't follow
9the ``u<N>-`` convention) keep working: they simply carry no unit sections and
10contribute nothing to the digest beyond their preamble.
11"""
12
13from __future__ import annotations
14
15import re
16from dataclasses import dataclass, field
17
18import yaml
19
20from orchestrator.grouping.plan_reader import strip_task_map
21
22_UNITS_HEADING = re.compile(r"^## Units[ \t]*$", re.MULTILINE)
23_H2_HEADING = re.compile(r"^## [ \t]*\S", re.MULTILINE)
24_UNIT_HEADING = re.compile(r"^### U(?P<num>\d+)\.[ \t]*(?P<rest>.*)$", re.MULTILINE)
25_BULLET = re.compile(r"^-\s+\*\*(?P<label>[^*]+)\*\*:\s?(?P<rest>.*)$")
26_TASK_MAP_BLOCK = re.compile(
27 r"```ya?ml[ \t]*\n(?P<body>[ \t]*# orchestrator-task-map v1[ \t]*\n.*?)```",
28 re.DOTALL,
29)
30_TASK_ID_UNIT_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^u(\d+)-")
31
32
33class PlanSectionsError(Exception):
34 """The plan's ``## Units`` structure doesn't cover every declared unit-id task."""
35
36
37@dataclass(frozen=True)
38class UnitSection:
39 unit_id: str # "u1", "u2", ... (matches the numeric part of the U<N> heading)
40 title: str # heading text after "### U<N>. "
41 text: str # verbatim section text (heading line through the next heading), found in source
42 summary: str
43 summary_is_fallback: bool
44 verification: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
45 implements: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
46 consumes: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
47
48
49@dataclass(frozen=True)
50class PlanSections:
51 preamble: str
52 units: dict[str, UnitSection]
53 digest: str
54 flags: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
55
56
57def unit_key_for_task(task_id: str) -> str | None:
58 """``u3-layered-context`` -> ``u3``; ``t1-scaffold`` -> ``None`` (not this
59 convention, no unit-section is expected for it)."""
60 match = _TASK_ID_UNIT_PREFIX.match(task_id)
61 return f"u{match.group(1)}" if match else None
62
63
64def section_for_task(units: dict[str, UnitSection], task_id: str) -> UnitSection | None:
65 key = unit_key_for_task(task_id)
66 return units.get(key) if key is not None else None
67
68
69def _declared_unit_task_ids(plan_text: str) -> list[str]:
70 """Best-effort extraction of ``task_id`` values from the plan's own embedded
71 task map, used only to cross-check unit-heading coverage. A malformed or
72 absent map raises nothing here — ``plan_reader.parse_task_map`` is the
73 authority on map validity; this is purely an auxiliary read."""
74 match = _TASK_MAP_BLOCK.search(plan_text)
75 if not match:
76 return []
77 try:
78 payload = yaml.safe_load(match.group("body"))
79 except yaml.YAMLError:
80 return []
81 if not isinstance(payload, dict):
82 return []
83 tasks = payload.get("tasks")
84 if not isinstance(tasks, list):
85 return []
86 return [
87 task["task_id"]
88 for task in tasks
89 if isinstance(task, dict) and isinstance(task.get("task_id"), str)
90 ]
91
92
93def _split_bullets(body: str) -> dict[str, str]:
94 """Top-level ``- **Label**: value`` bullets, continuation lines folded in."""
95 fields: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
96 current: str | None = None
97 for line in body.splitlines():
98 match = _BULLET.match(line)
99 if match:
100 current = match.group("label").strip()
101 fields[current] = [match.group("rest")]
102 elif current is not None:
103 fields[current].append(line)
104 return {label: "\n".join(lines).strip() for label, lines in fields.items()}
105
106
107def _parse_verification_items(raw: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
108 """``raw`` is the folded value of the ``Verification`` bullet: either a single
109 sentence, or a sub-bullet list (one item per ``- ``, continuation lines
110 joined into the same item)."""
111 lines = [line.strip() for line in raw.splitlines() if line.strip()]
112 if not lines or lines == ["—"]:
113 return ()
114 if not lines[0].startswith("- "):
115 return (" ".join(lines),)
116 bullets: list[str] = []
117 current: list[str] = []
118 for line in lines:
119 if line.startswith("- "):
120 if current:
121 bullets.append(" ".join(current))
122 current = [line[2:].strip()]
123 else:
124 current.append(line)
125 if current:
126 bullets.append(" ".join(current))
127 return tuple(bullets)
128
129
130def _parse_tags(text: str) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]:
131 implements: list[str] = []
132 consumes: list[str] = []
133 for keyword, bucket in (("implements", implements), ("consumes", consumes)):
134 for match in re.finditer(rf"{keyword}\b([^;]*)", text, re.IGNORECASE):
135 bucket.extend(re.findall(r"`([^`]+)`", match.group(1)))
136 return tuple(dict.fromkeys(implements)), tuple(dict.fromkeys(consumes))
137
138
139def _build_unit_section(num: str, heading_rest: str, text: str, flags: list[str]) -> UnitSection:
140 unit_id = f"u{num}"
141 title = heading_rest.strip()
142 body_after_heading = "\n".join(text.splitlines()[1:])
143 bullets = _split_bullets(body_after_heading)
144
145 summary_raw = bullets.get("Summary", "").strip()
146 if summary_raw and summary_raw != "—":
147 summary, is_fallback = summary_raw, False
148 else:
149 summary, is_fallback = title, True
150 flags.append(
151 f"plan-sections: unit {unit_id} has no 'Summary:' line — "
152 f"falling back to its heading title ({title!r})"
153 )
154
155 verification = _parse_verification_items(bullets.get("Verification", ""))
156 implements, consumes = _parse_tags(bullets.get("Implements / Consumes", ""))
157
158 return UnitSection(
159 unit_id=unit_id,
160 title=title,
161 text=text,
162 summary=summary,
163 summary_is_fallback=is_fallback,
164 verification=verification,
165 implements=implements,
166 consumes=consumes,
167 )
168
169
170def _build_digest(preamble: str, units: dict[str, UnitSection]) -> str:
171 ordered = sorted(units.values(), key=lambda u: int(u.unit_id[1:]))
172 lines = [preamble.rstrip("\n"), "", "## Unit summaries"]
173 for unit in ordered:
174 lines.append(f"- {unit.unit_id.upper()} ({unit.title}) Summary: {unit.summary}")
175 lines.append("")
176 lines.append("## Implements / Consumes registry")
177 any_tags = False
178 for unit in ordered:
179 if unit.implements:
180 lines.append(f"- {unit.unit_id.upper()} implements: {', '.join(unit.implements)}")
181 any_tags = True
182 if unit.consumes:
183 lines.append(f"- {unit.unit_id.upper()} consumes: {', '.join(unit.consumes)}")
184 any_tags = True
185 if not any_tags:
186 lines.append("- (none)")
187 return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
188
189
190def parse_plan_sections(plan_text: str) -> PlanSections:
191 """Split ``plan_text`` into its preamble, per-unit sections, and digest.
192
193 Deterministic and pure: the same text always yields byte-identical output.
194 """
195 units_match = _UNITS_HEADING.search(plan_text)
196 if units_match is None:
197 preamble = strip_task_map(plan_text)
198 return PlanSections(preamble=preamble, units={}, digest=_build_digest(preamble, {}))
199
200 preamble = strip_task_map(plan_text[: units_match.start()])
201
202 next_h2 = _H2_HEADING.search(plan_text, units_match.end())
203 units_span_end = next_h2.start() if next_h2 else len(plan_text)
204 units_span = plan_text[units_match.start() : units_span_end]
205
206 headings = list(_UNIT_HEADING.finditer(units_span))
207 flags: list[str] = []
208 units: dict[str, UnitSection] = {}
209 for index, match in enumerate(headings):
210 section_end = headings[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(headings) else len(units_span)
211 section_text = units_span[match.start() : section_end]
212 unit = _build_unit_section(match.group("num"), match.group("rest"), section_text, flags)
213 units[unit.unit_id] = unit
214
215 missing = [
216 task_id
217 for task_id in _declared_unit_task_ids(plan_text)
218 if (key := unit_key_for_task(task_id)) is not None and key not in units
219 ]
220 if missing:
221 raise PlanSectionsError(
222 "plan sections: missing '### U<N>.' heading for task id(s): " + ", ".join(missing)
223 )
224
225 return PlanSections(
226 preamble=preamble,
227 units=units,
228 digest=_build_digest(preamble, units),
229 flags=tuple(flags),
230 )

1"""Tests for deterministic spec assembly (plan U2) — the write_specs replacement."""
2
3import re
4
5import pytest
6
7from orchestrator.grouping.assembler import (
8 ASSEMBLED_FLAG,
9 AssemblyError,
10 AssemblyInputs,
11 assemble_group_specs,
12)
13from orchestrator.grouping.graphing import TaskGraph
14from orchestrator.grouping.plan_sections import parse_plan_sections

16PLAN = """# feat: toy plan
17
18## Units
19
20### U1. scaffold — create the app skeleton
21
22- **Goal**: Create the app skeleton.
23- **Summary**: Creates the app skeleton.
24- **Files**: `app/main.py` *(new)*
25- **Depends-on**: —
26- **Slice**: —
27- **Implements / Consumes**: implements `scaffold-ready`
28- **Verification**: `app/main.py` exists.
29
30### U2. items-api — items API routes
31
32- **Goal**: Items API routes.
33- **Summary**: Items API routes on the scaffold.
34- **Files**: `app/items.py` *(new)*
35- **Depends-on**: u1-scaffold
36- **Slice**: items
37- **Implements / Consumes**: consumes `scaffold-ready`; implements `/api/items`
38- **Verification**:
39 - `GET /api/items` returns 200.
40 - `POST /api/items` creates an item.
41
42### U3. items-ui — items admin page
43
44- **Goal**: Items admin page.
45- **Summary**: Items admin page calling the items API.
46- **Files**: `web/items.tsx` *(new)*
47- **Depends-on**: u1-scaffold
48- **Slice**: items
49- **Implements / Consumes**: consumes `/api/items`
50- **Verification**: the items page renders a table.
51
52## Task Map
53
54```yaml
55# orchestrator-task-map v1
56tasks:
57 - task_id: u1-scaffold
58 description: create the app skeleton
59 - task_id: u2-items-api
60 description: items API routes
61 depends_on: [u1-scaffold]
62 - task_id: u3-items-ui
63 description: items admin page
64 depends_on: [u1-scaffold]
65```
66"""
67
68PLAN_NO_VERIFICATION_U3 = PLAN.replace(
69 "- **Verification**: the items page renders a table.", "- **Verification**: —"
70)
71
72
73def make_graph(dependencies, metadata=None):
74 nodes = frozenset({"u1-scaffold", "u2-items-api", "u3-items-ui"})
75 return TaskGraph(
76 nodes=nodes,
77 dependencies=dependencies,
78 metadata=metadata or {},
79 )
80
81
82def make_inputs(plan_text=PLAN):
83 plan_sections = parse_plan_sections(plan_text)
84 graph = make_graph(
85 dependencies={("u1-scaffold", "u2-items-api"): 1.0, ("u1-scaffold", "u3-items-ui"): 1.0},
86 metadata={
87 "u1-scaffold": {"slice": None},
88 "u2-items-api": {"slice": "items"},
89 "u3-items-ui": {"slice": "items"},
90 },
91 )
92 partition = {"u1-scaffold": 0, "u2-items-api": 1, "u3-items-ui": 1}
93 members_by_gid = {0: ["u1-scaffold"], 1: ["u2-items-api", "u3-items-ui"]}
94 dag = {0: {1}}
95 descriptions = {
96 "u1-scaffold": "create the app skeleton",
97 "u2-items-api": "items API routes",
98 "u3-items-ui": "items admin page",
99 }
100 return AssemblyInputs(
101 plan_sections=plan_sections,
102 graph=graph,
103 partition=partition,
104 dag=dag,
105 members_by_gid=members_by_gid,
106 descriptions=descriptions,
107 group_label=lambda gid: f"g{gid + 1}",
108 )
109
110
111class TestAssembleGroupSpecs:
112 def test_every_group_gets_non_empty_contract_fields(self):
113 specs = assemble_group_specs(make_inputs())
114 assert set(specs) == {"g1", "g2"}
115 for spec in specs.values():
116 assert spec.name
117 assert spec.summary
118 assert spec.spec
119 assert spec.verification
120
121 def test_spec_contains_member_unit_sections_verbatim(self):
122 specs = assemble_group_specs(make_inputs())
123 sections = parse_plan_sections(PLAN)
124 assert sections.units["u1"].text in specs["g1"].spec
125 assert sections.units["u2"].text in specs["g2"].spec
126 assert sections.units["u3"].text in specs["g2"].spec
127 # g1 must not carry g2's member sections and vice versa
128 assert sections.units["u2"].text not in specs["g1"].spec
129
130 def test_relational_header_names_upstream_and_downstream_groups(self):
131 specs = assemble_group_specs(make_inputs())
132 assert "g2" in specs["g1"].spec.split("Downstream groups:")[1].split("Slice:")[0]
133 assert "g1" in specs["g2"].spec.split("Upstream groups:")[1].split("Downstream groups:")[0]
134
135 def test_regenerating_after_changed_partition_changes_the_header(self):
136 """R2: the header is graph/DAG facts, so a different partition must
137 produce a different header (here: no dependency edge crosses groups)."""
138 inputs = make_inputs()
139 no_dag_inputs = AssemblyInputs(
140 plan_sections=inputs.plan_sections,
141 graph=inputs.graph,
142 partition=inputs.partition,
143 dag={},
144 members_by_gid=inputs.members_by_gid,
145 descriptions=inputs.descriptions,
146 group_label=inputs.group_label,
147 )
148 specs_with_dag = assemble_group_specs(inputs)
149 specs_without_dag = assemble_group_specs(no_dag_inputs)
150 assert specs_with_dag["g1"].spec != specs_without_dag["g1"].spec
151
152 def test_verification_ids_match_pattern_and_cover_every_bullet(self):
153 specs = assemble_group_specs(make_inputs())
154 all_items = [item for spec in specs.values() for item in spec.verification]
155 assert len(all_items) == 4 # 1 (u1) + 2 (u2) + 1 (u3)
156 for item in all_items:
157 assert re.match(r"^g\d+-\d+$", item.id)
158 assert item.required is True
159 descriptions = {item.description for item in all_items}
160 assert "`app/main.py` exists." in descriptions
161 assert "`GET /api/items` returns 200." in descriptions
162 assert "`POST /api/items` creates an item." in descriptions
163 assert "the items page renders a table." in descriptions
164
165 def test_missing_unit_verification_fails_naming_the_unit(self):
166 with pytest.raises(AssemblyError, match="u3"):
167 assemble_group_specs(make_inputs(PLAN_NO_VERIFICATION_U3))
168
169 def test_byte_deterministic_across_two_calls(self):
170 a = assemble_group_specs(make_inputs())
171 b = assemble_group_specs(make_inputs())
172 assert {gid: spec.model_dump() for gid, spec in a.items()} == {
173 gid: spec.model_dump() for gid, spec in b.items()
174 }
175

177class TestAssembledFlag:
178 def test_flag_text_is_stable(self):
179 assert ASSEMBLED_FLAG == "specs: assembled from plan — speccer LLM skipped"

g2: cycle-repair-withdrawal

u10: cycle-repair-withdrawal — group-DAG repair withdraws inferred edges before merging (C4.1/R11)

Plan section U10

U10. cycle-repair-withdrawal — group-DAG repair withdraws inferred edges before merging (C4.1/R11)

  • Goal: repair_cycles receives the declared-edge set (the mapper's depends_on pairs) and, when a group-SCC cycle forms, first withdraws inferred precedence edges (banking their weight as affinity, as _drop_inferred_cycles already does at task level) until the group DAG is acyclic — falling back to the existing merge+re-split only if withdrawal alone cannot break the cycle. Declared edges are never withdrawn. Withdrawals are recorded in the trace repairs with the edges named.
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/partition.py, orchestrator/grouping/graphing.py, orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py, tests/test_partition.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: u9-partition-diagnostics
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • A fixture whose group cycle is closed only by an inferred edge partitions cleanly with no merge, the withdrawal recorded in the trace, and the final group count unchanged from the pre-cycle expectation.
    • A fixture whose cycle consists solely of declared edges still takes the merge+re-split path, and declared edges never appear as withdrawn in any trace.
Spec given to this group

Implement U10 (u10-cycle-repair-withdrawal) from the plan — fix C4.1/R11. Read that unit section for the goal.

Depends on u9-partition-diagnostics, which exposes the declared-vs-inferred edge classification; build on that rather than re-deriving it.

Today _drop_inferred_cycles (orchestrator/grouping/graphing.py:626) withdraws inferred edges at the task-graph level, but the group-DAG repair repair_cycles (orchestrator/grouping/partition.py) only merges SCCs and re-splits by wave — it never withdraws. That merge is what collapses a partition when a single inferred edge closes a group cycle.

Give repair_cycles the declared-edge set (the mapper's depends_on pairs) and, when a group-SCC cycle forms, first withdraw inferred precedence edges — banking their weight as affinity exactly as _drop_inferred_cycles already does at task level — until the group DAG is acyclic. Fall back to the existing merge + re-split only if withdrawal alone cannot break the cycle. Declared edges are never withdrawn, under any pressure. Record every withdrawal in the trace repairs with the edges named.

Scope guard. The plan is explicit that R11 is edge withdrawal only. The hyperedge / hub-routing re-modeling of symbol-derived edges is parked in the post-eval-harness backlog — do not start it, and do not change how symbol edges are created at graphing time.

Determinism discipline is unchanged: sorted iteration, a full ordering, byte-stable partitions.

Done means both fixtures below pass and tests/test_partition.py and the existing partition suite are green.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

u11: advisory-report — `group --advise`: one graph, all granularities, cohesion diagnostics (R12–R14)

Plan section U11

U11. advisory-report — group --advise: one graph, all granularities, cohesion diagnostics (R12–R14)

  • Goal: group --advise <plan> builds the task graph once (reusing the compute_partition prefix refactored into a graph-building seam), runs the partition at every GRANULARITY_LEVELS preset off that cached graph, and writes an Advisory Report — JSON artifact in the grouping's preview/ dir plus a human-readable rendering — containing per preset: group count, per-group node work and budget utilization (mean/max), cross-group edge cut, group-DAG depth, simulated makespan (_simulate_makespan), modularity (scorecard._modularity), with Pareto-dominant presets flagged. Cohesion diagnostics, zero LLM: weakly-connected components computed before Louvain (a multi-component or near-disconnected plan is flagged "this reads as N separate plans", naming the task sets); a seriality signal (critical path / max wave width via _compute_waves) plus a topological-order cut sweep whose valleys name candidate phase boundaries ("this reads as serial phases"); and a "structurally monolithic" report when modularity is low and every cut has high conductance. Thresholds are named module constants. --advise follows preview semantics: never touches a persisted groups.json.
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/advisory.py (new, large), orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py, orchestrator/grouping/partition.py, orchestrator/grouping/scorecard.py, orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_advisory.py (new, large)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: —
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: implements advisory-report
  • Verification:
    • group --advise on a fixture plan performs exactly one graph build (asserted via a counting client stub) and emits a report with one entry per granularity preset, each carrying group count, utilization, edge cut, DAG depth, makespan, and modularity.
    • A fixture of two disjoint task sets is flagged "reads as 2 separate plans" naming both sets; a pure chain fixture is flagged serial with the boundary between its widest-gap waves; a clique fixture reports "structurally monolithic".
    • After --advise, a pre-existing groups.json in the same grouping dir is byte-identical, and advisory.json lives under preview/.
    • The report is byte-deterministic across two runs on an unchanged repo.
Spec given to this group

Implement U11 (u11-advisory-report) from the plan — R12–R14, the core of wave 1c. Read that unit section for the authoritative goal; it is the largest unit in this run.

Add group --advise <plan>. It builds the task graph once — refactor the compute_partition prefix (orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py:436) into a graph-building seam so the graph can be built and then partitioned repeatedly — and runs the partition at every GRANULARITY_LEVELS preset (orchestrator/grouping/partition.py:40) off that cached graph. Per the plan's decision there is no cross-invocation cache in v1: reuse within a single invocation only, measure re-run latency, cache later only if it proves necessary.

Write an Advisory Report — a JSON artifact in the grouping's preview/ dir plus a human-readable rendering — carrying, per preset: group count, per-group node work and budget utilization (mean/max), cross-group edge cut, group-DAG depth, simulated makespan via _simulate_makespan (partition.py:783), and modularity via scorecard._modularity. Flag Pareto-dominant presets.

Cohesion diagnostics, zero LLM:

  • Weakly-connected components computed before Louvain; a multi-component or near-disconnected plan is flagged "this reads as N separate plans", naming the task sets.
  • A seriality signal — critical path over max wave width, using _compute_waves (partition.py:998) — plus a topological-order cut sweep whose valleys name candidate phase boundaries ("this reads as serial phases").
  • A "structurally monolithic" report when modularity is low and every cut has high conductance.

All four thresholds (near-disconnected WCC edge weight, seriality depth/width ratio, cut-sweep valley detection, low-modularity/high-conductance) are named module constants, tuned during implementation against the existing runs and traces in this repo. Justify each chosen value in a comment.

--advise follows the preview/ quarantine semantics already used by --no-spec/--dry-run (orchestrator/cli.py:665–742): it must never touch a persisted groups.json. No LLM call anywhere in this path.

This group is upstream of the plan-skill group, which teaches /orchestrator-plan to run --advise and present its diagnostics — keep the human-readable rendering presentable as-is.

Done means tests/test_advisory.py covers the one-build assertion, the three shape fixtures, preview isolation, and determinism.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

orchestrator/grouping/advisory.py
@@ -0,0 +1,587 @@
1"""`group --advise` (plan U11, R12-R14): one graph build, every granularity
2preset, cohesion diagnostics — zero LLM calls, never touches ``groups.json``.
3
4The whole point of this module is that it never calls the mapper/codegraph
5work more than once per invocation: ``build_partition_graph`` (pipeline.py's
6R19 seam) runs a single time, and every ``GRANULARITY_LEVELS`` preset below
7partitions the *same* ``TaskGraph`` object. Partitioning itself (Louvain,
8lift, split, merge, repair) is pure Python over that in-memory graph, so
9running it three times costs milliseconds, not more codegraph subprocesses.
10
11Preview semantics (plan U8's ``preview/`` quarantine, reused unchanged): the
12CLI writes this module's output only under ``preview/advisory.json`` and
13never touches a persisted ``groups.json`` — see ``_cmd_group``'s ``--advise``
14branch.
15"""
16

41)

45# --------------------------------------------------------------------- tuning
46#
47# All four thresholds below are named module constants (plan U11's own
48# requirement, so the advisory report's judgment calls are visible and
49# adjustable in one place, not buried in expressions). Each is justified
50# against this repo's own edge-weight/estimator conventions rather than
51# picked arbitrarily; "tune in 1c" (the plan's decision) means these are
52# expected to move as the eval harness (R20, out of scope here) accumulates
53# more real runs to check them against — nothing here claims to be final.
54
55# WCC-before-Louvain (R13): an affinity edge weaker than the *weakest* signal
56# the edge-weight model can produce (EdgeWeights.semantic_floor = 0.5, plan
57# U... graphing.py) does not meaningfully bridge two clusters — pruning
58# edges at or below that floor and re-checking connectivity is what turns a
59# single weakly-connected component into a "near-disconnected" one. Declared
60# dependency edges are never pruned: they are required precedence, not a soft
61# affinity signal, so they can never make a plan read as "separate" no matter
62# how weak their weight.
63NEAR_DISCONNECTED_EDGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD = 0.5
64
65# Seriality (critical path / max wave width): a plan whose longest dependency
66# chain is at least twice as long as its widest wave has, by construction,
67# more depth than breadth — most of the plan's tasks are waiting on a
68# predecessor rather than running in parallel with siblings. 2.0 is the point
69# where "somewhat serial" tips into "this plan reads as serial phases" rather
70# than "a DAG with some structure"; a plan that is one task wide throughout
71# (a pure chain) scores arbitrarily high above this, a balanced fan-out/fan-in
72# DAG scores at or below 1.0.
73SERIALITY_DEPTH_WIDTH_RATIO_THRESHOLD = 2.0
74
75# Cut-sweep valley detection: a candidate phase boundary is a topological-order
76# split whose crossing dependency-edge count is a strict local minimum (fewer
77# edges cross here than on either side) — the sweep's natural "waist" points.
78# No magnitude threshold is applied on top of the local-minimum test itself:
79# any strict local minimum is reported, since a valley that fails to be one
80# is already excluded by construction; the module constant exists so the
81# comparison is named rather than an inline `<` at each call site, and so a
82# future revision that *does* want a magnitude floor has one place to add it.
83CUT_SWEEP_VALLEY_MARGIN = 0
84
85# "Structurally monolithic": modularity below this is Newman's own rule of
86# thumb for "no meaningful community structure" (values above roughly 0.3-0.7
87# indicate real cluster structure in practice; this repo's own healthy
88# partitions score well above 0.1 per grouping-metrics.jsonl history) — so
89# 0.1 is a conservative floor, not a guess. Paired with conductance: even the
90# *best* achievable cut (minimum over the whole topological sweep) must leave
91# most of the smaller side's connections crossing it (0.6) for the plan to be
92# called monolithic — a plan is only flagged when neither Louvain nor any
93# ordered bipartition finds a good split.
94MONOLITHIC_MODULARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.1
95MONOLITHIC_CONDUCTANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.6
96

148def build_advisory_report(
149 plan_path: Path,
150 repo_root: Path,
151 config: OrchestratorConfig | None = None,
152 llm_runner: JsonRunner | None = None,
153 client: CodegraphClient | None = None,
154 allow_unknown_symbols: bool = False,
155 progress: ProgressFn | None = None,
156) -> AdvisoryReport:
157 """Build the task graph once, partition it at every granularity preset,
158 and compute the cohesion diagnostics — the whole ``--advise`` pipeline.
159
160 No cross-invocation cache (plan U11 decision): a second call rebuilds the
161 graph from scratch. Reuse is within this one call only.
162 """
163 config = config or OrchestratorConfig()
164 llm_runner = llm_runner or functools.partial(
165 claude_json_runner, model=config.session.speccer_model
166 )
167 client = client or CodegraphClient(repo_root=repo_root)
168
169 build = build_partition_graph(
170 plan_path=plan_path,
171 repo_root=repo_root,
172 config=config,
173 llm_runner=llm_runner,
174 client=client,
175 allow_unknown_symbols=allow_unknown_symbols,
176 progress=progress,
177 )
178 graph = build.graph
179 node_work_map = {
180 node: node_work(graph.metadata.get(node, {}), config.estimator) for node in graph.nodes
181 }
182
183 def node_work_fn(node: str) -> float:
184 return node_work_map[node]
185
186 _emit(progress, "stage: advise")
187 presets: list[GranularityMetrics] = []
188 raw_metrics: dict[Granularity, dict] = {}
189 for level in GRANULARITY_LEVELS:
190 strategy = DefaultPartitionStrategy(
191 work_fn=node_work_fn,
192 budget_cap=build.budget_cap,
193 hub_threshold=config.partition.hub_threshold,
194 louvain_resolution=config.partition.louvain_resolution,
195 granularity=level,
196 )
197 partition = strategy.partition(graph)
198 dag = build_group_dag(graph, partition)
199 raw_metrics[level] = _preset_metrics(graph, partition, dag, node_work_map, build.budget_cap)
200
201 pareto = _pareto_dominant(raw_metrics)
202 for level in GRANULARITY_LEVELS:
203 metrics = raw_metrics[level]
204 presets.append(
205 GranularityMetrics(
206 granularity=level,
207 group_count=metrics["group_count"],
208 node_work_fraction_mean=metrics["node_work_fraction_mean"],
209 node_work_fraction_max=metrics["node_work_fraction_max"],
210 cross_group_edge_cut=metrics["cross_group_edge_cut"],
211 group_dag_depth=metrics["group_dag_depth"],
212 simulated_makespan=metrics["simulated_makespan"],
213 modularity=metrics["modularity"],
214 pareto_dominant=pareto[level],
215 )
216 )
217
218 cohesion = _cohesion_diagnostics(graph, node_work_map)
219
220 from orchestrator.grouping.pipeline import _portable_path
221
222 return AdvisoryReport(
223 plan_path=_portable_path(plan_path, repo_root),
224 granularities=presets,
225 cohesion=cohesion,
226 )
