229# ------------------------------------------------------------- per-preset
230
231
232def _preset_metrics(
233 graph: TaskGraph,
234 partition: Partition,
235 dag: dict[int, set[int]],
236 node_work_map: Mapping[str, float],
237 budget_cap: float,
238) -> dict:
239 groups: dict[int, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
240 for node, gid in partition.items():
241 groups[gid].append(node)
242
243 fractions = [
244 (sum(node_work_map.get(n, 0.0) for n in members) / budget_cap if budget_cap else 0.0)
245 for members in groups.values()
246 ]
247 cross_group_edge_cut = sum(
248 1 for up, down in graph.dependencies if partition[up] != partition[down]
249 )
250 return {
251 "group_count": len(groups),
252 "node_work_fraction_mean": (sum(fractions) / len(fractions)) if fractions else 0.0,
253 "node_work_fraction_max": max(fractions) if fractions else 0.0,
254 "cross_group_edge_cut": cross_group_edge_cut,
255 "group_dag_depth": _dag_depth(dag, set(groups)),
256 "simulated_makespan": _simulate_makespan(graph, partition, node_work_map),
257 "modularity": _modularity(graph, partition),
258 }
259
260
261def _dag_depth(dag: Mapping[int, set[int]], gids: set[int]) -> int:
262 """Same longest-chain computation as ``scorecard._longest_group_chain``,
263 duplicated rather than imported (it is private there and this module
264 should not reach into another module's underscore names)."""
265 predecessors_of: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
266 for up, downs in dag.items():
267 for down in downs:
268 predecessors_of[down].append(up)
269
270 memo: dict[int, int] = {}
271
272 def depth(gid: int) -> int:
273 if gid in memo:
274 return memo[gid]
275 preds = predecessors_of.get(gid, ())
276 memo[gid] = 1 + max((depth(p) for p in preds), default=0)
277 return memo[gid]
278
279 return max((depth(gid) for gid in gids), default=0)
280
281
282# Objective direction per metric used to rank presets (R14): "better" always
283# means "closer to what an operator running the group would want" — fewer
284# cross-group edges to coordinate, a shallower serialization depth, a lower
285# simulated makespan, higher modularity (cleaner clusters), and higher mean
286# utilization of the budget cap (less headroom wasted). All five are used
287# together so a preset that merely inflates one number cannot look dominant.
288_MINIMIZE = ("cross_group_edge_cut", "group_dag_depth", "simulated_makespan")
289_MAXIMIZE = ("modularity", "node_work_fraction_mean")
290
291
292def _pareto_dominant(raw_metrics: Mapping[Granularity, dict]) -> dict[Granularity, bool]:
293 def dominates(a: dict, b: dict) -> bool:
294 at_least_as_good = all(a[k] <= b[k] for k in _MINIMIZE) and all(
295 a[k] >= b[k] for k in _MAXIMIZE
296 )
297 strictly_better = any(a[k] < b[k] for k in _MINIMIZE) or any(a[k] > b[k] for k in _MAXIMIZE)
298 return at_least_as_good and strictly_better
299
300 result = {}
301 for level, metrics in raw_metrics.items():
302 dominated = any(
303 dominates(other, metrics)
304 for other_level, other in raw_metrics.items()
305 if other_level != level
306 )
307 result[level] = not dominated
308 return result
309
310
311# ------------------------------------------------------------- cohesion
312
313
314def _undirected_affinity_graph(graph: TaskGraph) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
315 """Weighted undirected adjacency over affinity only — the same scope
316 ``_louvain``/``_modularity`` cluster over, so conductance and modularity
317 are judging the same structure."""
318 adjacency: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {node: {} for node in graph.nodes}
319 for (a, b), w in graph.affinity.items():
320 if w <= 0:
321 continue
322 adjacency[a][b] = adjacency[a].get(b, 0.0) + w
323 adjacency[b][a] = adjacency[b].get(a, 0.0) + w
324 return adjacency
325
326
327def _combined_adjacency(
328 graph: TaskGraph, *, min_affinity_weight: float = 0.0
329) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
330 """Undirected connectivity over affinity (weight-thresholded) plus
331 dependencies (never thresholded — declared precedence is always
332 structural, never a "weak" signal)."""
333 adjacency: dict[str, set[str]] = {node: set() for node in graph.nodes}
334 for (a, b), w in graph.affinity.items():
335 if w < min_affinity_weight:
336 continue
337 adjacency[a].add(b)
338 adjacency[b].add(a)
339 for a, b in graph.dependencies:
340 adjacency[a].add(b)
341 adjacency[b].add(a)
342 return adjacency
343
344
345def _weakly_connected_components(adjacency: Mapping[str, set[str]]) -> list[list[str]]:
346 visited: set[str] = set()
347 components: list[list[str]] = []
348 for start in sorted(adjacency):
349 if start in visited:
350 continue
351 component = []
352 queue = [start]
353 while queue:
354 node = queue.pop(0)
355 if node in visited:
356 continue
357 visited.add(node)
358 component.append(node)
359 queue.extend(nb for nb in sorted(adjacency.get(node, ())) if nb not in visited)
360 components.append(sorted(component))
361 return sorted(components, key=lambda c: c[0] if c else "")
362
363
364def _topo_order(graph: TaskGraph) -> list[str]:
365 """Nodes ordered by ascending dependency wave, tie-broken by name — a
366 valid topological order for the cut sweep below."""
367 waves = _compute_waves(graph)
368 return sorted(graph.nodes, key=lambda n: (waves[n], n))
369
370
371def _cut_dependency_count(graph: TaskGraph, prefix: set[str], suffix: set[str]) -> int:
372 return sum(1 for up, down in graph.dependencies if up in prefix and down in suffix)
373
374
375def _conductance(
376 prefix: set[str], suffix: set[str], adjacency: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]]
377) -> float:
378 def volume(side: set[str]) -> float:
379 return sum(sum(adjacency.get(n, {}).values()) for n in side)
380
381 cut = sum(w for n in prefix for nb, w in adjacency.get(n, {}).items() if nb in suffix)
382 vol_prefix, vol_suffix = volume(prefix), volume(suffix)
383 denom = min(vol_prefix, vol_suffix)
384 if denom <= 0:
385 return 1.0 # no internal structure to preserve on the smaller side: worst-case cut
386 return cut / denom
387
388
389@dataclass
390class _SweepPoint:
391 index: int
392 prefix: list[str]
393 suffix: list[str]
394 dependency_cut: int
395 conductance: float
396
397
398def _cut_sweep(graph: TaskGraph, order: list[str], affinity_adjacency: dict) -> list[_SweepPoint]:
399 points = []
400 for i in range(1, len(order)):
401 prefix, suffix = order[:i], order[i:]
402 points.append(
403 _SweepPoint(
404 index=i,
405 prefix=prefix,
406 suffix=suffix,
407 dependency_cut=_cut_dependency_count(graph, set(prefix), set(suffix)),
408 conductance=_conductance(set(prefix), set(suffix), affinity_adjacency),
409 )
410 )
411 return points
412
413
414def _valleys(points: list[_SweepPoint]) -> list[_SweepPoint]:
415 """Strict local minima of the cut-count sweep (R13's "cut-sweep valleys"):
416 a point whose crossing-edge count is lower than both neighbors names a
417 candidate phase boundary. Boundary points (the sweep's first/last split)
418 qualify too when they are lower than their one neighbor."""
419 valleys = []
420 for i, point in enumerate(points):
421 left = points[i - 1].dependency_cut if i > 0 else None
422 right = points[i + 1].dependency_cut if i + 1 < len(points) else None
423 lower_than_left = left is None or point.dependency_cut < left - CUT_SWEEP_VALLEY_MARGIN
424 lower_than_right = right is None or point.dependency_cut < right - CUT_SWEEP_VALLEY_MARGIN
425 if lower_than_left and lower_than_right and (left is not None or right is not None):
426 valleys.append(point)
427 return valleys
428
429
430def _cohesion_diagnostics(
431 graph: TaskGraph, node_work_map: Mapping[str, float]
432) -> list[CohesionFinding]:
433 if not graph.nodes:
434 return []
435
436 findings: list[CohesionFinding] = []
437
438 full_adjacency = _combined_adjacency(graph)
439 full_components = _weakly_connected_components(full_adjacency)
440 pruned_adjacency = _combined_adjacency(
441 graph, min_affinity_weight=NEAR_DISCONNECTED_EDGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD
442 )
443 pruned_components = _weakly_connected_components(pruned_adjacency)
444
445 if len(full_components) > 1:
446 findings.append(
447 CohesionFinding(
448 kind="disconnected",
449 message=(
450 f"this reads as {len(full_components)} separate plans — no task "
451 "in one set shares a dependency or affinity edge with any task "
452 "in another"
453 ),
454 task_sets=full_components,
455 )
456 )
457 elif len(pruned_components) > 1:
458 findings.append(
459 CohesionFinding(
460 kind="disconnected",
461 message=(
462 f"this reads as {len(pruned_components)} separate plans — the "
463 "only edges bridging these task sets are weaker than a single "
464 f"shared-file link (weight < {NEAR_DISCONNECTED_EDGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD})"
465 ),
466 task_sets=pruned_components,
467 )
468 )
469
470 waves = _compute_waves(graph)
471 critical_path_length = max(waves.values()) + 1 if waves else 0
472 width_by_wave: dict[int, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
473 for node, wave in waves.items():
474 width_by_wave[wave].append(node)
475 max_wave_width = max((len(members) for members in width_by_wave.values()), default=0)
476 seriality_ratio = (critical_path_length / max_wave_width) if max_wave_width else 0.0
477
478 order = _topo_order(graph)
479 affinity_adjacency = _undirected_affinity_graph(graph)
480 points = _cut_sweep(graph, order, affinity_adjacency) if len(order) > 1 else []
481
482 if seriality_ratio >= SERIALITY_DEPTH_WIDTH_RATIO_THRESHOLD:
483 work_by_wave = {
484 wave: sum(node_work_map.get(n, 0.0) for n in members)
485 for wave, members in width_by_wave.items()
486 }
487 ordered_waves = sorted(work_by_wave)
488 boundary_wave = ordered_waves[0]
489 boundary_gap = -1.0
490 for a, b in zip(ordered_waves, ordered_waves[1:]):
491 gap = abs(work_by_wave[b] - work_by_wave[a])
492 if gap > boundary_gap:
493 boundary_gap = gap
494 boundary_wave = a
495 findings.append(
496 CohesionFinding(
497 kind="serial",
498 message=(
499 f"this reads as serial phases — the critical path ({critical_path_length} "
500 f"waves) is {seriality_ratio:.1f}x the widest wave ({max_wave_width} tasks); "
501 f"the widest work gap falls between wave {boundary_wave} and wave "
502 f"{boundary_wave + 1}"
503 ),
504 boundary={
505 "critical_path_length": critical_path_length,
506 "max_wave_width": max_wave_width,
507 "boundary_after_wave": boundary_wave,
508 "tasks_before": sorted(width_by_wave.get(boundary_wave, [])),
509 "tasks_after": sorted(width_by_wave.get(boundary_wave + 1, [])),
510 },
511 )
512 )
513 valleys = _valleys(points)
514 if valleys:
515 findings.append(
516 CohesionFinding(
517 kind="serial",
518 message=(
519 f"{len(valleys)} candidate phase boundary(ies) found by the "
520 "topological cut sweep — the fewest dependency edges cross "
521 "the plan at these splits"
522 ),
523 boundary={
524 "valleys": [
525 {
526 "after_index": v.index,
527 "dependency_cut": v.dependency_cut,
528 "tasks_before": v.prefix,
529 "tasks_after": v.suffix,
530 }
531 for v in valleys
532 ]
533 },
534 )
535 )
536
537 has_affinity = any(w > 0 for w in graph.affinity.values())
538 if points and has_affinity:
539 # No affinity edges at all (a plan whose tasks share nothing but
540 # dependency order) has no clustering structure to judge in the first
541 # place — that is a pure-sequencing plan, not a monolithic one, so the
542 # diagnostic is skipped rather than reporting the vacuous "cut leaves
543 # everything on one side" conductance of an edgeless graph.
544 best = min(points, key=lambda p: p.conductance)
545 graph_modularity = _best_effort_modularity(graph)
546 if (
547 graph_modularity < MONOLITHIC_MODULARITY_THRESHOLD
548 and best.conductance > MONOLITHIC_CONDUCTANCE_THRESHOLD
549 ):
550 findings.append(
551 CohesionFinding(
552 kind="monolithic",
553 message=(
554 "this reads as structurally monolithic — modularity "
555 f"({graph_modularity:.3f}) is below {MONOLITHIC_MODULARITY_THRESHOLD} and "
556 f"even the best cut leaves conductance {best.conductance:.2f} "
557 f"(above {MONOLITHIC_CONDUCTANCE_THRESHOLD}); no natural split exists"
558 ),
559 boundary={
560 "modularity": graph_modularity,
561 "best_cut_conductance": best.conductance,
562 "best_cut_after_index": best.index,
563 },
564 )
565 )
566
567 return findings
568
569
570def _best_effort_modularity(graph: TaskGraph) -> float:
571 """Modularity of the graph's own best clustering, independent of any
572 chosen granularity preset — Louvain communities over the affinity graph,
573 the same clustering ``partition.py`` itself would produce with no hubs
574 or slices in play."""
575 import networkx as nx
576
577 from orchestrator.grouping.partition import LOUVAIN_SEED
578
579 g = nx.Graph()
580 g.add_nodes_from(graph.nodes)
581 for (a, b), w in graph.affinity.items():
582 if w > 0:
583 g.add_edge(a, b, weight=w)
584 if g.number_of_edges() == 0:
585 return 0.0
586 communities = nx.community.louvain_communities(g, weight="weight", seed=LOUVAIN_SEED)
587 return nx.algorithms.community.quality.modularity(g, communities, weight="weight")

1"""Tests for orchestrator/grouping/advisory.py — `group --advise` (plan U11).
2
3Every fixture here is a bare task-map plan (no `## Units`) so `parse_task_map`
4takes the deterministic fast path and no `symbols:` field is ever declared, so
5no codegraph call beyond sync/quiescence/files fires — the whole pipeline is
6exercised with zero LLM calls and a tiny, countable set of codegraph calls.
7"""

17 CUT_SWEEP_VALLEY_MARGIN,

19 MONOLITHIC_MODULARITY_THRESHOLD,
20 NEAR_DISCONNECTED_EDGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD,
21 SERIALITY_DEPTH_WIDTH_RATIO_THRESHOLD,
22 build_advisory_report,
23 serialize_advisory_report,
24)
25from orchestrator.grouping.graphing import CodegraphClient

27 compute_partition,
28 run_grouping,

33def _stub_codegraph_runner(args):
34 if args[0] == "sync":
35 return ""
36 if args[0] == "files":
37 return "stub repo\n"
38 if args[0] == "status":
39 return json.dumps(
40 {
41 "initialized": True,
42 "fileCount": 1,
43 "nodeCount": 1,
44 "edgeCount": 0,
45 "pendingChanges": {"added": 0, "modified": 0, "removed": 0},
46 }
47 )
48 if args[0] == "query":
49 return "[]"
50 raise AssertionError(f"unexpected codegraph call in a fixture test: {args}")
51
52
53def _counting_runner(counter: list):
54 def runner(args):
55 counter.append(tuple(args))
56 return _stub_codegraph_runner(args)
57
58 return runner

62 raise AssertionError(f"LLM must not be called for a task-mapped plan: {schema.get('title')}")

66 return f"# feat: {title}\n\n## Task Map\n\n```yaml\n# orchestrator-task-map v1\ntasks:\n{tasks_yaml}```\n"

69# A tree of uneven branches converging on one leaf (test_partition.py's own
70# `_granularity_ladder_graph` shape): independent/balanced/monolithic produce
71# different group counts and metrics, so the granularity comparison and its
72# Pareto flags have something real to compare.
73LADDER_PLAN = _task_map_plan(
74 """\
75 - task_id: root
76 description: root
77 files: [app/root.py]
78 - task_id: alpha1
79 description: alpha1
80 files: [app/alpha1.py]
81 depends_on: [root]
82 - task_id: alpha2
83 description: alpha2
84 files: [app/alpha2.py]
85 depends_on: [alpha1]
86 - task_id: beta1
87 description: beta1
88 files: [app/beta1.py]
89 depends_on: [root]
90 - task_id: beta2
91 description: beta2
92 files: [app/beta2.py]
93 depends_on: [beta1]
94 - task_id: beta3
95 description: beta3
96 files: [app/beta3.py]
97 depends_on: [beta2]
98 - task_id: gamma1
99 description: gamma1
100 files: [app/gamma1.py]
101 depends_on: [root]
102 - task_id: leaf
103 description: leaf
104 files: [app/leaf.py]
105 depends_on: [alpha2, beta3, gamma1]
106""",
107 title="ladder",
108)
109
110# Two disjoint chains: no shared files, no depends_on between the two sets —
111# nothing at all bridges group {a1, a2} and group {b1, b2}.
112DISJOINT_PLAN = _task_map_plan(

116 files: [app/a1.py]
117 - task_id: a2
118 description: a2

125 description: b2
126 files: [app/b2.py]
127 depends_on: [b1]
128""",
129 title="disjoint",
130)

132# A pure 5-node dependency chain: one task per wave, so critical path (5) is

134CHAIN_PLAN = _task_map_plan(

148 description: c4
149 files: [app/c4.py]
150 depends_on: [c3]
151 - task_id: c5
152 description: c5
153 files: [app/c5.py]
154 depends_on: [c4]
155""",
156 title="chain",
157)

160# uniform-weight affinity clique with no natural split.
161CLIQUE_PLAN = _task_map_plan(

165 files: [app/shared.py]

167 description: m2
168 files: [app/shared.py]
169 - task_id: m3
170 description: m3
171 files: [app/shared.py]
172 - task_id: m4
173 description: m4
174 files: [app/shared.py]
175 - task_id: m5
176 description: m5
177 files: [app/shared.py]
178""",
179 title="clique",
180)

231 assert preset.group_count > 0
232 assert preset.node_work_fraction_mean >= 0
233 assert preset.node_work_fraction_max >= 0
234 assert preset.cross_group_edge_cut >= 0
235 assert preset.group_dag_depth >= 1
236 assert preset.simulated_makespan >= 0
237 assert isinstance(preset.modularity, float)

239 # candidates and objectives that trade off (fewer groups vs. more
240 # cross-group coordination), it is never the case that every preset
241 # loses to some other on every axis.

g4: merge-fill-penalty

u12: fill-penalty — merge key prefers balanced fills over cap-filling (R19b experiment)

Plan section U12

U12. fill-penalty — merge key prefers balanced fills over cap-filling (R19b experiment)

  • Goal: The merge key in merge_small_groups gains a fill/balance term ranked above merged_work's current 5th place: candidate merges whose merged work lands inside a target band (config knob [partition] target_fill_ratio, default chosen and justified in-code) are preferred over ones landing at the cap, so one group no longer absorbs merges until it hits the cap. Determinism discipline preserved (sorted iteration, full ordering). The granularity-ladder and hub tests are updated where the expected partitions legitimately change; any change is explained in the test.
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/partition.py, orchestrator/config.py, tests/test_partition.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: —
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • A synthetic fixture reproducing the greedy pathology (one group absorbing every merge to ~96% of cap while siblings starve) now yields a partition whose per-group fill variance is strictly lower, with no group over cap and the group DAG still acyclic.
    • Partitions remain byte-deterministic across runs, and slice must-link and budget-cap invariants hold on the whole existing test suite.
Spec given to this group

Implement U12 (u12-fill-penalty) from the plan — the R19b greedy-fragmentation experiment, landed in wave 1c by user decision. Read that unit section for the goal.

The merge key in merge_small_groups is today (-source_wave, candidate_makespan, -removed_affinity, -edge_weight, merged_work, source, target) (orchestrator/grouping/partition.py:974) — merged_work sits in 5th place with no fill or balance term, which is the measured cause of one group absorbing merges until it hits ~96% of cap while siblings starve.

Add a fill/balance term ranked above merged_work's current position: candidate merges whose merged work lands inside a target band are preferred over ones landing at the cap. The band comes from a new config knob [partition] target_fill_ratio in orchestrator/config.py. Its default is a judgment call — choose it, and justify the choice in-code; the plan records that calibrating it properly is backlogged to the eval harness, so a defensible default with a comment is the deliverable, not a tuned optimum.

Determinism discipline is non-negotiable: sorted iteration, a full ordering with no ties left to hash order, byte-stable partitions across runs. Slice must-link and budget-cap invariants must continue to hold across the whole existing suite.

The granularity-ladder and hub tests will legitimately shift where the expected partition changes. Update them — and explain in the test why the new partition is the right one. Do not pin a test to an old partition you believe is worse, and do not loosen an assertion to make it pass.

The advisory report's granularity comparison (a sibling group) is the intended before/after readout for this change; if it is available, record the observed shift.

Done means the pathology fixture shows strictly lower fill variance, no group over cap, an acyclic group DAG, and tests/test_partition.py plus the full suite green.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

730class TestFillPenalty:
731 """Plan U12 (R19b): the merge key's fill/balance term.
732
733 ``target_fill_ratio=0.0`` reproduces the pre-U12 key byte-for-byte: the
734 new term becomes ``abs(merged_work - 0.0) == merged_work``, sitting right
735 next to the existing ``merged_work`` field with an identical value, so it
736 can never change the total order — that is how these tests get an "old
737 key" oracle without duplicating the merge loop.
738 """
739
740 def _pathology_graph(self):
741 """Two hubs, each independently a valid dependency for a pool of
742 eight small (0.3) and one large (2.0) shared task — modelling a
743 greedy first-fit pathology: whichever hub the loop happens to favour
744 first can keep absorbing the cheapest remaining task every round
745 (old key: plain ``merged_work`` ascending always prefers the
746 numerically smallest candidate), landing two same-sized ~2.0 lumps
747 while its sibling hub never receives a single merge. ``granularity=
748 "balanced"`` is required for more than one small task to ever join
749 the same hub (the default ``independent`` guard treats same-parent
750 siblings as parallel and refuses to merge more than one in)."""
751 nodes = ["hub_a", "hub_b"] + [f"s{i}" for i in range(1, 9)] + ["big"]
752 deps = {}
753 for n in [f"s{i}" for i in range(1, 9)] + ["big"]:
754 deps[("hub_a", n)] = 1.0
755 deps[("hub_b", n)] = 1.0
756 work = {"hub_a": 0.2, "hub_b": 0.2, "big": 2.0}
757 work.update({f"s{i}": 0.3 for i in range(1, 9)})
758 g = graph(nodes, dependencies=deps)
759 return g, work

U5 — the authoring contract, in skills/orchestrator-plan/SKILL.md and docs/orchestrator-task-map.md:

  • The required per-unit tagged Summary: line (R21) and the ### U<N>. ↔ u<N>-… id convention.
  • Verification written as a bulleted list, one item per bullet; a single-line Verification is one item.
  • symbols is optional, contributes derived precedence, and on a dense codebase omitting it may give a better partition. This replaces the current unconditional "Record exact existing symbols" instruction — the measured lesson (R9/C4) is that populating symbols on this codebase added 103 inferred edges and degenerated the partition; declared depends_on and shared-file affinity carry the structure instead.

Never split silently, never rewrite the plan prose. Proceed-as-one must be an explicit option in the question.

Do not fabricate wave-2 capability. The mechanical split (R16) and the deepen command (R17) do not exist yet; note them as arriving with wave 2 and do not reference a deepen command as currently runnable.

Done means both documents state the conventions above and the skill's hand-off phase reads as specified.

101## Pricing a task's node work
102
103Each task's **node work**, in tokens, is:
104
105```
106node_work = source_bytes / 4.0 × 1.3 + per-file allowance
107```
108
109- `source_bytes / 4.0` — existing files' bytes converted to tokens at
110 `bytes_per_token` (4.0).
111- `× 1.3` — `slack_multiplier`, applied to the byte-derived estimate.
112- **per-file allowance** — each existing file adds `per_file_tool_allowance`
113 (2,000 tokens, the tool-output overhead of reading it); each prospective
114 file adds its `size_hints` class price (`small` 500, `medium` 2,000,
115 `large` 5,000) or the same flat 2,000 default if unhinted.
116
117A group's (and a slice's) **budget cap** is the token budget minus a fixed
118head:
119
120```
121cap = 200,000 − head
122head = (base_tokens + spec_tokens_allowance) × 1.3 × 2.5
123```
124
125`base_tokens` is the size of the shared base context every worker forks from;
126`spec_tokens_allowance` is the assembled-spec budget; `2.5` is
127`coder_slack_multiplier`, converting read-cost tokens into the coder-session
128peak the cap actually guards (a coder iterates, so its real usage runs well
129above a single read pass). Node work is scaled by the same `2.5` before it is
130compared against the cap, so both sides of the comparison are in coder
131tokens.
132
133These are today's defaults (`orchestrator/grouping/estimator.py`,
134`orchestrator/config.py`) — check `group --price <plan>` for the actual
135resolved values and a sub-second, per-task breakdown against the cap before

No worker context contains the full plan document. Byte-stability and the task-map-absence guarantees carry over to the digest. base_tokens/budget_cap now derive from the digest-based context (groups get roomier; no compensation is applied).

  • Symbols: —

  • Verification:

    • A group consuming /api/x implemented by another group carries a contracts line naming /api/x and the implementing task id, and does not contain that neighbor unit's section body.
    • The union of one group's assembled spec plus the base context contains that group's full unit sections exactly once.

Implement U3 (u3-layered-context) from the plan — the token-economy half of wave 1a (R22/R23). Read that unit section for the authoritative goal.

This group depends on u1-plan-sections and u2-spec-assembly (delivered by the spec-assembly group): the digest builder and the assembler already exist when you start. Your job is to switch the two consumers over.

compile_base_context (orchestrator/grouping/base_context.py:19) currently ends with strip_task_map(plan) — the full plan text. Replace that with the U1 digest: preamble + per-unit tagged Summary: lines + implements/consumes registry. Everything else in the base context (ground rules, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, codegraph summary) stays. The byte-stability contract and the guarantee that no orchestrator-task-map marker survives both carry over to the digest — this content feeds start_base (orchestrator/execution/sessions.py:400), the run's base session every worker forks from, so a byte drift is a cache miss for every worker.

The assembler gains contracts-only neighbor lines: for each cross-group unit this group consumes from or provides to, append one line carrying the contract tag, the counterpart task id, and that unit's Summary: line. Never a neighbor's full section. The invariant to hold: base context + one group's spec contains that group's own unit sections exactly once and no other group's bodies. No worker context anywhere contains the full plan document.

base_tokens and therefore partition_budget_cap now derive from the smaller digest-based context, so groups get roomier. Apply no compensating adjustment — the plan is explicit about this. Update tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py where cap expectations legitimately move, and say in the test why.

Layered context is the default, not a flag — do not add an opt-out that restores the full plan.

g7: speccer-removal

u4: speccer-removal — delete the grouping-time speccer in one recoverable commit

Plan section U4

U4. speccer-removal — delete the grouping-time speccer in one recoverable commit

  • Goal: Remove orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py, orchestrator/prompts/speccer.md, the grouping-form model knob (GroupingOptions.model_speccer in orchestrator/observatory/launch.py and its argv plumbing, the grouping-form parts of ui/src/routes/Launch.tsx, ui/src/components/launch/ExecutionOptions.tsx, ui/src/types.ts, ui/src/api.ts), and the grouping-time speccer wiring/help-text in orchestrator/cli.py (_speccer_json_runner stays for the mapper and rewrite speccer; its docstring and --model-speccer help are reworded to "mapper / rewrite speccer"). The mid-run rewrite speccer, the run-form model_speccer knob, and the SpeccerCalls viewer stay untouched. This unit's changes land as one standalone commit whose sha is recorded in a short "grouping-time speccer removed" note in docs/orchestrator-grouping.md (recovery = cherry-pick, per ADR 0006).
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py, orchestrator/prompts/speccer.md, orchestrator/cli.py, orchestrator/observatory/launch.py, ui/src/routes/Launch.tsx, ui/src/components/launch/ExecutionOptions.tsx, ui/src/types.ts, ui/src/api.ts, docs/orchestrator-grouping.md, tests/test_observatory_launch.py, ui/src/routes/launch.test.tsx
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: u2-spec-assembly
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • grep -r "write_specs\|prompts/speccer" orchestrator/ ui/src/ finds no references; orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py and orchestrator/prompts/speccer.md do not exist.
    • The grouping launch API rejects/ignores model_speccer for groupings while the run launch body still accepts it, and pytest tests/test_observatory_launch.py plus the UI test suite pass.
    • The rewrite-speccer path still works: orchestrator/execution/review.py's rewrite flow and its tests are unchanged and green.
    • docs/orchestrator-grouping.md contains a removal note with a commit sha.
Spec given to this group

Implement U4 (u4-speccer-removal) from the plan, and read ADR 0006 (docs/adr/0006-delete-the-grouping-time-speccer.md) for the decision behind it. This group depends on u2-spec-assembly: the deterministic assembler is already the live path, so nothing calls write_specs by the time you delete it.

Delete: orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py, orchestrator/prompts/speccer.md, the grouping-form model knob (GroupingOptions.model_speccer in orchestrator/observatory/launch.py around lines 121/147 and its argv plumbing, the grouping-form parts of ui/src/routes/Launch.tsx:193, ui/src/components/launch/ExecutionOptions.tsx, ui/src/types.ts around line 532, ui/src/api.ts), and the grouping-time speccer wiring and help text in orchestrator/cli.py.

Keep — this is the sharp edge of the unit. Two speccers exist. The mid-run rewrite speccer stays untouched: orchestrator/cli.py:1919 _rewrite_provider area, the escalation path in orchestrator/execution/review.py, and the run-form model_speccer knob in ui/src/components/launch/ExecutionOptions.tsx:261. The Observatory LLM-call viewer (SpeccerCalls in ui/src/components/grouping/GroupingTab.tsx) stays. _speccer_json_runner stays — it also serves the mapper for foreign plans; reword its docstring and the --model-speccer help to "mapper / rewrite speccer". config.session.speccer_model and the --model-speccer flag survive; only the grouping-time consumer goes.

Land this unit's changes as one standalone commit and record its sha in a short "grouping-time speccer removed" note in docs/orchestrator-grouping.md — recovery is a cherry-pick, per ADR 0006.

Done means no references remain, the grouping launch API no longer accepts model_speccer while the run launch body still does, and tests/test_observatory_launch.py, ui/src/routes/launch.test.tsx, the rest of the UI suite, and the review/rewrite tests are green.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

2026 """Ask the rewrite speccer LLM for a name/summary/spec/verification for every
2027 skeleton group (one group, in practice — the mid-run rewrite seam).
2028

2030 the deterministic facts the prose must cover. Output must cover exactly the
2031 given group ids."""
2032 prompt = Template(load_template("rewrite_speccer")).substitute(
2033 plan_text=plan_text,

2037 def validate(payload: dict) -> dict[str, GroupSpec]:
2038 entries = payload["groups"]
2039 if not isinstance(entries, list):
2040 raise ValueError("'groups' must be a list")
2041 try:
2042 specs = [GroupSpec.model_validate(entry) for entry in entries]
2043 except ValidationError as exc:
2044 raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc
2045 got = {spec.group_id for spec in specs}
2046 expected = set(skeletons)
2047 if got != expected:
2048 raise ValueError(f"group ids mismatch: expected {sorted(expected)}, got {sorted(got)}")
2049 return {spec.group_id: spec for spec in specs}
2050
2051 return call_llm_json(
2052 runner,
2053 prompt,
2054 _REWRITE_SPEC_SCHEMA,
2055 validate=validate,
2056 max_retries=max_retries,
2057 failure_dir=failure_dir,
2058 recorder=recorder,
2059 )

54class GroupSpec(BaseModel):
55 group_id: str
56 name: str
57 summary: str = Field(max_length=SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS)
58 spec: str
59 verification: list[VerificationItem] = Field(default_factory=list)

62def write_specs(
63 plan_text: str,
64 skeletons: dict[str, dict],
65 runner: JsonRunner,
66 max_retries: int = 2,
67 failure_dir: Path | None = None,
68 recorder: LlmCallRecorder | None = None,
69) -> dict[str, GroupSpec]:
70 """Ask the LLM for names/summaries/specs/verification for every skeleton group.
71
72 ``skeletons`` maps group_id → {tasks, descriptions, files} — the deterministic
73 facts the prose must cover. Output must cover exactly the given group ids.
74 """
75 prompt = Template(load_template("speccer")).substitute(
76 plan_text=plan_text,
77 groups_json=json.dumps(skeletons, indent=2, sort_keys=True),
78 )
79
80 def validate(payload: dict) -> dict[str, GroupSpec]:
81 entries = payload["groups"]
82 if not isinstance(entries, list):
83 raise ValueError("'groups' must be a list")
84 try:
85 specs = [GroupSpec.model_validate(entry) for entry in entries]
86 except ValidationError as exc:
87 raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc
88 got = {spec.group_id for spec in specs}
89 expected = set(skeletons)
90 if got != expected:
91 raise ValueError(f"group ids mismatch: expected {sorted(expected)}, got {sorted(got)}")
92 return {spec.group_id: spec for spec in specs}
93
94 return call_llm_json(
95 runner,
96 prompt,
97 SPECCER_SCHEMA,
98 validate=validate,
99 max_retries=max_retries,
100 failure_dir=failure_dir,
101 recorder=recorder,
102 )

g8: error-accumulation

u6: error-accumulation — every validation phase reports all its failures (C1/R5)

Plan section U6

U6. error-accumulation — every validation phase reports all its failures (C1/R5)

  • Goal: _check_slice_overflow collects every over-cap slice and raises once listing all of them; plan_reader accumulates shape errors and reports them together, then accumulates reference errors (unknown depends_on, bad size_hints, duplicate ids) and reports them together — phase order preserved, first failing phase reports its full set then stops. Error text keeps naming each problem exactly as today (one line per problem).
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py, orchestrator/grouping/plan_reader.py, tests/test_plan_reader.py, tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: —
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • A map with three over-cap slices fails with one GrouperError naming all three slices with their sums and overshoots.
    • A map with two unknown-key tasks and two bad size_hints entries reports both unknown-key problems in one error; fixing those then reports both size_hints problems in one error.
    • Single-error behavior is unchanged in wording for existing tests.
Spec given to this group

Implement U6 (u6-error-accumulation) from the plan — fix C1/R5, the measured failure where validating one written plan cost 15 group invocations because each run surfaced exactly one error. Read that unit section for the goal.

Two sites. _check_slice_overflow (orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py:214) raises on the first over-cap slice inside its loop; collect every over-cap slice and raise once listing all of them with their sums and overshoots. orchestrator/grouping/plan_reader.py has roughly twenty raise TaskMapError sites and no accumulator; group them into phases and accumulate within each — shape errors reported together first, then reference errors (unknown depends_on, bad size_hints, duplicate ids) reported together.

Phase order is preserved: the first failing phase reports its full set and stops. Do not merge phases into one mega-report — a reference check on a malformed map produces noise, which is why the phasing exists.

Error text keeps naming each problem exactly as it does today, one line per problem, so single-error wording is unchanged and existing tests that assert on messages keep passing without edits. This is a legibility change, not a wording rewrite.

This group is upstream of the budget-naming and partition-diagnostics groups, which both build on the accumulator — keep the accumulation helper reusable and clearly named rather than inlining it twice.

Done means tests/test_plan_reader.py and tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py cover multi-error reporting per phase and the full suite is green.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

1"""Shared multi-error accumulation for grouping validation phases (plan U6).
2
3Grouping validation runs in phases — slice-overflow checking, task-map shape,
4task-map cross-references — and each phase used to raise on the first problem
5it found. On a written plan with several independent problems in one phase,
6that cost one `group` invocation per problem (C1/R5) instead of one per phase.
7``ErrorAccumulator`` collects every problem a phase finds and raises them
8together; phase order stays the caller's responsibility — call ``raise_all``
9at the end of one phase before starting the next, so a later phase never runs
10against input a still-failing earlier phase already condemned.
11"""
12
13from __future__ import annotations
14
15
16class ErrorAccumulator:
17 """Collects problem messages for one validation phase.
18
19 A single accumulated message raises with its own wording unchanged, so
20 single-error call sites keep their existing exact text; two or more join
21 into one report listing each verbatim.
22 """
23
24 def __init__(self) -> None:
25 self._messages: list[str] = []
26
27 def add(self, message: str) -> None:
28 self._messages.append(message)
29
30 def __bool__(self) -> bool:
31 return bool(self._messages)
32
33 def __len__(self) -> int:
34 return len(self._messages)
35
36 def raise_all(self, exc_type: type[Exception]) -> None:
37 """Raise ``exc_type`` with every accumulated message, or do nothing."""
38 if not self._messages:
39 return
40 if len(self._messages) == 1:
41 raise exc_type(self._messages[0])
42 detail = "\n".join(f" - {message}" for message in self._messages)
43 raise exc_type(f"{len(self._messages)} problems found:\n{detail}")

g9: price-mode

u7: price-mode — `group --price` prints the budget arithmetic sub-second (C3/R6)

Plan section U7

U7. price-mode — group --price prints the budget arithmetic sub-second (C3/R6)

  • Goal: group --price <plan> parses the task map (no graph build, no codegraph client, no quiescence), prices every task's node work from working tree byte counts + size_hints, and prints: per-task node work, per-slice sums against the cap with pass/fail, and the resolved budget parameters (token_budget, multipliers, per-file allowance, head, cap) — with the cap labeled approximate (compiled with an empty codegraph summary) and the approximation stated. Exits non-zero if any slice exceeds the cap. Runs sub-second.
  • Files: orchestrator/cli.py, orchestrator/grouping/estimator.py, tests/test_cli_price.py (new, medium)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: —
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: consumes planning-contract
  • Verification:
    • On a fixture plan with one over-cap slice, --price exits non-zero, prints that slice's member-by-member node work, sum, cap, and overshoot, and never invokes codegraph (asserted via a client stub that raises).
    • On this repo's 2026-08-26 plan document, --price completes in under one second and its per-task figures match grouping-trace.json node_work for the same map within the stated cap approximation.
    • The output names both node work and coder work scales consistently with U8.
Spec given to this group

Implement U7 (u7-price-mode) from the plan — fix C3/R6, giving a plan author a sub-second way to price a task map before paying for a full group run. Read that unit section for the goal.

Add group --price <plan> to orchestrator/cli.py, with any pricing helpers it needs in orchestrator/grouping/estimator.py. It parses the task map only — no graph build, no codegraph client, no quiescence check — prices every task's node work from working-tree byte counts plus size_hints, and prints per-task node work, per-slice sums against the cap with pass/fail, and the resolved budget parameters (token_budget, bytes_per_token, slack_multiplier, coder_slack_multiplier, per_file_tool_allowance, head, cap).

The cap is approximate and must say so. Per the plan's decision, --price compiles its base context with an empty codegraph summary, so the printed cap lands within a few thousand tokens of the real one while staying sub-second. Print the approximation and its cause in the output rather than burying it.

Exit non-zero if any slice exceeds the cap. Runtime must be under a second on this repo's real plan documents — that budget is the whole point of the mode, so avoid pulling in the graph-building path even indirectly.

Output vocabulary must name both node work and coder work consistently with U8 (a sibling group owns that unit; the two literal labels are the shared contract).

Done means tests/test_cli_price.py covers the over-cap exit path with a codegraph client stub that raises if touched, plus the timing and cross-check against grouping-trace.json.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

161def price_task_mappings(
162 mappings: list[TaskMapping],
163 repo_root: Path,
164 base_tokens: int,
165 config: EstimatorConfig,
166) -> PriceReport:
167 """Price every task mapping from working-tree byte counts (plan U7), with no
168 graph and no codegraph client — ``source_bytes_of`` and ``node_work`` both
169 read only the filesystem and plain config numbers.
170 """
171 task_prices: dict[str, TaskPrice] = {}
172 for mapping in mappings:
173 metadata = {
174 "source_bytes": source_bytes_of(repo_root, mapping.files),
175 "files": mapping.files,
176 "prospective_files": mapping.prospective_files,
177 "size_hints": dict(mapping.size_hints),
178 }
179 coder_work = node_work(metadata, config)
180 task_prices[mapping.task_id] = TaskPrice(
181 task_id=mapping.task_id,
182 slice=mapping.slice,
183 node_work=coder_work / config.coder_slack_multiplier,
184 coder_work=coder_work,
185 )
186
187 budget_cap = partition_budget_cap(base_tokens, config)
188 atoms: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
189 for mapping in mappings:
190 label = mapping.slice or mapping.task_id
191 atoms.setdefault(label, []).append(mapping.task_id)
192
193 slice_prices = []
194 for label, members in sorted(atoms.items()):
195 coder_work = sum(task_prices[m].coder_work for m in members)
196 node_work_sum = sum(task_prices[m].node_work for m in members)
197 slice_prices.append(
198 SlicePrice(
199 label=label,
200 tasks=tuple(sorted(members)),
201 node_work=node_work_sum,
202 coder_work=coder_work,
203 over_cap=coder_work > budget_cap,
204 )
205 )
206
207 head = (
208 (base_tokens + config.spec_tokens_allowance)
209 * config.slack_multiplier
210 * config.coder_slack_multiplier
211 )
212 return PriceReport(
213 tasks=tuple(task_prices[m.task_id] for m in sorted(mappings, key=lambda m: m.task_id)),
214 slices=tuple(slice_prices),
215 token_budget=config.token_budget,
216 bytes_per_token=config.bytes_per_token,
217 slack_multiplier=config.slack_multiplier,
218 coder_slack_multiplier=config.coder_slack_multiplier,
219 per_file_tool_allowance=config.per_file_tool_allowance,
220 base_tokens=base_tokens,
221 head=head,
222 budget_cap=budget_cap,
223 )
224
225
226def price_plan(plan_path: Path, repo_root: Path, config: OrchestratorConfig) -> PriceReport:
227 """``group --price <plan>`` (plan U7/C3): parses the task map and prices it
228 sub-second, with zero graph build and zero codegraph client — the whole
229 point of this mode. Raises ``TaskMapError`` if the plan carries no
230 embedded task map (this mode has no LLM-mapper fallback to fall back to).
231 """
232 plan_text = plan_path.read_text()
233 mappings = parse_task_map_for_pricing(plan_text, repo_root)
234 if mappings is None:
235 raise TaskMapError(
236 "plan has no embedded orchestrator-task-map block — --price requires a "
237 "task-mapped plan (see docs/orchestrator-task-map.md); the LLM mapper "
238 "has no sub-second, zero-codegraph equivalent"
239 )
240 base_context = compile_base_context(repo_root, plan_path, "")
241 base_tokens = int(len(base_context) / config.estimator.bytes_per_token)
242 return price_task_mappings(mappings, repo_root, base_tokens, config.estimator)

135def parse_task_map_for_pricing(plan_text: str, repo_root: Path) -> list[TaskMapping] | None:
136 """``group --price`` (plan U7): the same file/prospective/size_hints split as
137 ``parse_task_map``, but against the filesystem directly instead of a
138 ``CodegraphClient`` — pricing never needs ``symbols`` (they carry no weight
139 in ``estimator.node_work``), so this skips symbol verification entirely
140 rather than requiring a live index. ``None`` if the plan carries no task map
141 block, mirroring ``parse_task_map``.
142 """
143 blocks = _BLOCK.findall(plan_text)
144 if not blocks:
145 versions = _ANY_VERSION.findall(plan_text)
146 if versions:
147 raise TaskMapError(
148 f"unsupported task map version v{versions[0]} (this parser reads v1)"
149 )
150 return None
151 if len(blocks) > 1:
152 raise TaskMapError("multiple orchestrator-task-map blocks; exactly one is allowed")
153
154 try:
155 payload = yaml.safe_load(blocks[0])
156 except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
157 raise TaskMapError(f"task map is not valid YAML: {exc}") from exc
158 tasks = _validate_shape(payload)
159
160 mappings: list[TaskMapping] = []
161 for entry in tasks:
162 task_id = entry["task_id"]
163 raw_size_hints: dict[str, str] = entry.get("size_hints") or {}
164 files: list[str] = []
165 prospective: list[str] = []
166 for file in _dedupe(entry.get("files") or []):
167 if (repo_root / file).is_file():
168 if file in raw_size_hints:
169 raise TaskMapError(
170 f"task {task_id!r} size_hints names {file!r}, which already exists — "
171 "hints price unwritten (prospective) work only"
172 )
173 files.append(file)
174 else:
175 prospective.append(file)
176 size_hints = tuple(
177 sorted((f, raw_size_hints[f]) for f in prospective if f in raw_size_hints)
178 )
179 mappings.append(
180 TaskMapping(
181 task_id,
182 files=tuple(files),
183 prospective_files=tuple(prospective),
184 size_hints=size_hints,
185 depends_on=tuple(_dedupe(entry.get("depends_on") or [])),
186 slice=entry.get("slice"),
187 )
188 )
189 return mappings
190

U8. budget-naming — one vocabulary for node work vs coder work (C2/R7)

  • Goal: Everywhere an operator sees a budget figure — the slice-overflow error, the dry-run/group report listing, --price output — the two quantities are named distinctly: node work (unscaled) and coder work (× coder_slack_multiplier). The slice-overflow error prints both figures and states the multiplier. No arithmetic changes.
  • Files: orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py, orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: u6-error-accumulation
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • The slice-overflow error message contains both a node work and a coder work figure for each offending slice and the literal multiplier value in use.

Spec given to this group

Implement U8 (u8-budget-naming) from the plan — fix C2/R7, where an operator reading a budget figure cannot tell whether it is the unscaled quantity or the coder-scaled one. Read that unit section for the goal.

Depends on u6-error-accumulation: the slice-overflow error already reports all offending slices when you start, so you are changing the wording of a multi-slice message.

Everywhere an operator sees a budget figure — the slice-overflow error in orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py, the dry-run/group report listing, and the --price output — name the two quantities distinctly: node work for the unscaled figure (node_work, orchestrator/grouping/estimator.py:51) and coder work for the figure scaled by coder_slack_multiplier (2.5). The slice-overflow error prints both figures per offending slice and states the multiplier value in use.

No arithmetic changes. This is vocabulary only — partition_budget_cap, node_work, and the head computation are untouched. No user-facing output may say a bare "work" for either quantity.

The --price command is built by a sibling group; that unit's own verification requires its output to name both scales consistently with this one. Establish the vocabulary here as the reference — if the two land in either order, the shared constraint is the two literal labels node work and coder work.

Done means tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py asserts the labels and the multiplier in the overflow message, and the suite is green.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

(a) Provenance in the degenerate-partition error. When the partition degenerates into one SCC, report how many of the edges inside the offending SCC are inferred versus declared, with the inferred edges' source kind — e.g. "103 of 127 dependency edges are inferred from symbols". Source this from the same contribution data EdgeProvenanceRecorder/edge_provenance_document (orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py:306) already records; do not build a second provenance channel. This is the diagnostic that would have explained the measured case where populating symbols on this dense codebase added 103 inferred precedence edges and collapsed the partition.

(b) Slice re-entry detection. A dependency path that leaves a slice and re-enters it is currently only visible as saturation. Detect it on the contracted graph before partitioning and report by name with the exact edit: "slice resilience contracts u1 and u3, but u1 → u2 → u3 leaves the slice and returns — bring u2 into the slice or drop the label". Report all such shapes together, per the R5 discipline.

Work spans pipeline.py, graphing.py, and partition.py; keep the detection in the layer that owns the contracted graph rather than duplicating traversal.

This group is upstream of the cycle-repair-withdrawal group, which consumes the declared-vs-inferred distinction — expose that classification as a reusable value, not just error-message text.

Done means fixtures for both shapes fail with the specific messages and tests/test_partition.py plus tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py are green.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the full plan document: every unit's section) — never another group's spec.

492class SliceReentryPath:
493 """A dependency path that leaves a declared slice and returns to it (plan
494 U9/C5): once the slice contracts to one supernode for Louvain, this is
495 exactly what closes a cycle that does not exist at task level, and it used
496 to surface only as a generic degenerate-partition saturation message with
497 no actionable edit. ``path`` runs slice member to slice member, in order,
498 naming every node in between.
499 """
500
501 slice: str
502 path: tuple[str, ...]
503
504
505def _find_path_leaving_and_returning(
506 start: str, member_set: set[str], successors: Mapping[str, list[str]]
507) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
508 """Shortest dependency path from ``start`` (a slice member), through nodes
509 outside the slice, back to another slice member — sorted BFS, so the
510 reported path is stable across runs."""
511 queue: deque[tuple[str, ...]] = deque([(start,)])
512 visited = {start}
513 while queue:
514 path = queue.popleft()
515 current = path[-1]
516 for nxt in sorted(successors.get(current, ())):
517 if nxt in member_set:
518 if nxt != start and len(path) > 1:
519 return (*path, nxt)
520 continue
521 if nxt in visited:
522 continue
523 visited.add(nxt)
524 queue.append((*path, nxt))
525 return None
526

528def find_slice_reentrant_paths(
529 graph: TaskGraph, atoms: dict[str, list[str]]
530) -> list[SliceReentryPath]:
531 """Detect, on the contracted graph, every slice a dependency path leaves
532 and re-enters (plan U9/C5) — the shape ``_contract_slices`` turns into a
533 cycle that does not exist at task level. The full task graph is already
534 required to be acyclic (``TaskGraph.assert_acyclic_dependencies``), so any
535 cycle introduced by contraction must pass through at least one slice
536 supernode; every slice whose supernode sits in such a cycle is reported
537 here (R5 discipline: the caller collects and raises all of them together),
538 each with one concrete path reconstructed from the original graph.
539 """
540 if not atoms:
541 return []
542 unit_graph, _self_loops, _unit_of = _contract_slices(graph, atoms)
543 adjacency: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
544 for up, down in unit_graph.dependencies:
545 adjacency[up].add(down)
546 sccs = _strongly_connected_components(adjacency, set(unit_graph.nodes))
547 cyclic_units = {unit for scc in sccs if len(scc) > 1 for unit in scc}
548
549 successors: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
550 for up, down in graph.dependencies:
551 successors[up].append(down)
552
553 results: list[SliceReentryPath] = []
554 for label, members in sorted(atoms.items()):
555 if f"slice::{label}" not in cyclic_units:
556 continue
557 member_set = set(members)
558 for start in sorted(members):
559 path = _find_path_leaving_and_returning(start, member_set, successors)
560 if path is not None:
561 results.append(SliceReentryPath(slice=label, path=path))
562 break
563 return results

1515 ones were inferred from — sourced from the same per-edge ledgers
1516 ``edge-provenance.json`` already records, not a second channel."""

1518 def _graph_with_provenance(self):
1519 from orchestrator.grouping.graphing import EdgeContribution, EdgeProvenance
1520 from orchestrator.grouping.partition import TaskGraph, canonical_pair
1521
1522 provenance = EdgeProvenance()
1523 provenance.record_dependency(
1524 ("a", "b"),
1525 EdgeContribution(kind="call", declared=False, scaled_weight=2.0),
1526 )
1527 provenance.record_dependency(
1528 ("a", "b"),
1529 EdgeContribution(kind="call", declared=False, scaled_weight=2.0),
1530 )
1531 provenance.record_dependency(
1532 ("b", "c"),
1533 EdgeContribution(kind="impact", declared=False, scaled_weight=1.5),
1534 )
1535 provenance.record_dependency(
1536 ("c", "a"),
1537 EdgeContribution(kind="declared_depends_on", declared=True, scaled_weight=1.0),
1538 )
1539 return TaskGraph(
1540 nodes=frozenset({"a", "b", "c"}),
1541 affinity={canonical_pair("a", "b"): 2.0, canonical_pair("b", "c"): 1.5},
1542 dependencies={("a", "b"): 2.0, ("b", "c"): 1.5, ("c", "a"): 1.0},
1543 provenance=provenance,
1544 )
1545
1546 def test_edge_provenance_counts_classify_declared_vs_inferred(self):
1547 from orchestrator.grouping.pipeline import _edge_provenance_counts
1548
1549 graph = self._graph_with_provenance()
1550 declared, inferred, inferred_kinds = _edge_provenance_counts(
1551 graph, (("a", "b"), ("b", "c"), ("c", "a"))
1552 )
1553 assert declared == 1
1554 assert inferred == 2
1555 assert inferred_kinds == {"call": 1, "impact": 1}

509class TestSliceReentry:

515 def test_run10_shape_is_detected_and_named(self):

562 ("v2", "v3"): 1.0,
563 },
564 slices={"u1": "alpha", "u3": "alpha", "v1": "beta", "v3": "beta"},

569 by_slice = {r.slice: r.path for r in results}

571 assert by_slice["beta"] == ("v1", "v2", "v3")
